170|    @staticmethod
171|    def _add_parser_option(
172|        section_group: argparse._ArgumentGroup, argument: _Argument
173|    ) -> None:
174|        """Add an argument."""
175|        if isinstance(argument, _StoreArgument):
176|            section_group.add_argument(
177|                *argument.flags,
178|                action=argument.action,
179|                default=argument.default,
180|                type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
181|                help=argument.help,
182|                metavar=argument.metavar,
183|                choices=argument.choices,
184|            )
185|        elif isinstance(argument, _StoreOldNamesArgument):
186|            section_group.add_argument(
187|                *argument.flags,
188|                **argument.kwargs,
189|                action=argument.action,
190|                default=argument.default,
191|                type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
192|                help=argument.help,
193|                metavar=argument.metavar,
194|                choices=argument.choices,
195|            )
196|            # We add the old name as hidden option to make it's default value gets loaded when
197|            # argparse initializes all options from the checker
198|            assert argument.kwargs["old_names"]
199|            for old_name in argument.kwargs["old_names"]:
200|                section_group.add_argument(
201|                    f"--{old_name}",
202|                    action="store",
203|                    default=argument.default,
204|                    type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
205|                    help=argparse.SUPPRESS,
206|                    metavar=argument.metavar,
207|                    choices=argument.choices,
208|                )
209|        elif isinstance(argument, _StoreNewNamesArgument):
210|            section_group.add_argument(
211|                *argument.flags,
212|                **argument.kwargs,
213|                action=argument.action,
214|                default=argument.default,
215|                type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
216|                help=argument.help,
217|                metavar=argument.metavar,
218|                choices=argument.choices,
219|            )
220|        elif isinstance(argument, _StoreTrueArgument):
221|            section_group.add_argument(
222|                *argument.flags,
223|                action=argument.action,
224|                default=argument.default,
225|                help=argument.help,
226|            )
227|        elif isinstance(argument, _CallableArgument):
228|            section_group.add_argument(
229|                *argument.flags,
230|                **argument.kwargs,
231|                action=argument.action,
232|                help=argument.help,
233|                metavar=argument.metavar,
234|            )
235|        elif isinstance(argument, _ExtendArgument):
236|            section_group.add_argument(
237|                *argument.flags,
238|                action=argument.action,
239|                default=argument.default,
240|                type=argument.type,  # type: ignore[arg-type] # incorrect typing in typeshed
241|                help=argument.help,
242|                metavar=argument.metavar,
243|                choices=argument.choices,
244|                dest=argument.dest,
245|            )
246|        else:
247|            raise UnrecognizedArgumentAction

390|    def optik_option(
391|        self, provider: ConfigProvider, opt: str, optdict: OptionDict
392|    ) -> tuple[list[str], OptionDict]:  # pragma: no cover
393|        """DEPRECATED: Get our personal option definition and return a suitable form for
394|        use with optik/optparse.

396|        warnings.warn(
397|            "optik_option has been deprecated. Parsing of option dictionaries should be done "
398|            "automatically by initializing an ArgumentsProvider.",
399|            DeprecationWarning,
400|        )
401|        optdict = copy.copy(optdict)
402|        if "action" in optdict:
403|            self._nocallback_options[provider] = opt
404|        else:
405|            optdict["action"] = "callback"
406|            optdict["callback"] = self.cb_set_provider_option
407|        # default is handled here and *must not* be given to optik if you
408|        # want the whole machinery to work
409|        if "default" in optdict:
410|            if (
411|                "help" in optdict
412|                and optdict.get("default") is not None
413|                and optdict["action"] not in ("store_true", "store_false")
414|            ):
415|                optdict["help"] += " [current: %default]"  # type: ignore[operator]
416|            del optdict["default"]
417|        args = ["--" + str(opt)]
418|        if "short" in optdict:
419|            self._short_options[optdict["short"]] = opt  # type: ignore[index]
420|            args.append("-" + optdict["short"])  # type: ignore[operator]
421|            del optdict["short"]
422|        # cleanup option definition dict before giving it to optik
423|        for key in list(optdict.keys()):
424|            if key not in self._optik_option_attrs:
425|                optdict.pop(key)
426|        return args, optdict

428|    def generate_config(
429|        self, stream: TextIO | None = None, skipsections: tuple[str, ...] = ()
430|    ) -> None:  # pragma: no cover
431|        """DEPRECATED: Write a configuration file according to the current configuration
432|        into the given stream or stdout.
433|        """
434|        warnings.warn(
435|            "generate_config has been deprecated. It will be removed in pylint 3.0.",
436|            DeprecationWarning,
437|        )
438|        options_by_section = {}
439|        sections = []
440|        for group in self._arg_parser._action_groups:
441|            group_name = group.title
442|            assert group_name
443|            if group_name in skipsections:
444|                continue
445|
446|            options = []
447|            option_actions = [
448|                i
449|                for i in group._group_actions
450|                if not isinstance(i, argparse._SubParsersAction)
451|            ]
452|            for opt in option_actions:
453|                if "--help" in opt.option_strings:
454|                    continue

456|                optname = opt.option_strings[0][2:]
457|
458|                try:
459|                    optdict = self._option_dicts[optname]
460|                except KeyError:

464|                    (
465|                        optname,
466|                        optdict,
467|                        getattr(self.config, optname.replace("-", "_")),
468|                    )
469|                )
470|
471|                options = [
472|                    (n, d, v) for (n, d, v) in options if not d.get("deprecated")
473|                ]
474|
475|            if options:
476|                sections.append(group_name)
477|                options_by_section[group_name] = options
478|        stream = stream or sys.stdout
479|        printed = False
480|        for section in sections:
481|            if printed:
482|                print("\n", file=stream)
483|            with warnings.catch_warnings():
484|                warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
485|                utils.format_section(
486|                    stream, section.upper(), sorted(options_by_section[section])
487|                )

531|            with open(config_file, encoding="utf_8_sig") as fp:
532|                parser.read_file(fp)
533|            # normalize each section's title
534|            for sect, values in list(parser._sections.items()):  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
535|                if sect.startswith("pylint."):
536|                    sect = sect[len("pylint.") :]
537|                if not sect.isupper() and values:

539|
540|        if verbose:

543|    @staticmethod
544|    def _parse_toml(
545|        config_file: Path, parser: configparser.ConfigParser
546|    ) -> None:  # pragma: no cover
547|        """DEPRECATED: Parse and handle errors of a toml configuration file.
548|
549|        TODO: 3.0: Remove deprecated method.
550|        """
551|        with open(config_file, mode="rb") as fp:
552|            content = tomllib.load(fp)
553|        try:
554|            sections_values = content["tool"]["pylint"]
555|        except KeyError:
556|            return
557|        for section, values in sections_values.items():
558|            section_name = section.upper()
559|            # TOML has rich types, convert values to
560|            # strings as ConfigParser expects.
561|            if not isinstance(values, dict):
562|                continue
563|            for option, value in values.items():
564|                if isinstance(value, bool):
565|                    values[option] = "yes" if value else "no"
566|                elif isinstance(value, list):
567|                    values[option] = ",".join(value)
568|                else:
569|                    values[option] = str(value)
570|            for option, value in values.items():
571|                try:
572|                    parser.set(section_name, option, value=value)
573|                except configparser.NoSectionError:
574|                    parser.add_section(section_name)
575|                    parser.set(section_name, option, value=value)

inherited-members should support more than one class
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I have two situations:
- A class inherits from multiple other classes. I want to document members from some of the base classes but ignore some of the base classes
- A module contains several class definitions that inherit from different classes that should all be ignored (e.g., classes that inherit from list or set or tuple). I want to ignore members from list, set, and tuple while documenting all other inherited members in classes in the module.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The :inherited-members: option to automodule should accept a list of classes. If any of these classes are encountered as base classes when instantiating autoclass documentation, they should be ignored.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to not use automodule, but instead manually enumerate several autoclass blocks for a module. This only addresses the second bullet in the problem description and not the first. It is also tedious for modules containing many class definitions.

111|            if lckey[0:1].isalpha() or lckey.startswith('_'):
112|                lckey = chr(127) + lckey
113|            # ensure a determinstic order *within* letters by also sorting on
114|            # the entry itself
115|            return (lckey, entry[0])
116|        newlist = sorted(new.items(), key=keyfunc)
117|
118|        if group_entries:
119|            # fixup entries: transform
120|            #   func() (in module foo)
121|            #   func() (in module bar)
122|            # into
123|            #   func()
124|            #     (in module foo)
125|            #     (in module bar)
126|            oldkey = ''
127|            oldsubitems = None  # type: Dict[str, List]
128|            i = 0
129|            while i < len(newlist):
130|                key, (targets, subitems, _key) = newlist[i]
131|                # cannot move if it has subitems; structure gets too complex
132|                if not subitems:

137|                            # previous entry

139|                                extend(targets)

155|            return key

157|        # group the entries by letter
158|        def keyfunc3(item: Tuple[str, List]) -> str:
159|            # hack: mutating the subitems dicts to a list in the keyfunc
160|            k, v = item
161|            v[1] = sorted(((si, se) for (si, (se, void, void)) in v[1].items()),

170|                else:

172|                    return _('Symbols')
173|            else:
174|                return v[2]
175|        return [(key_, list(group))
176|                for (key_, group) in groupby(newlist, keyfunc3)]

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Generate man page section directories
**Current man page generation does not conform to `MANPATH` search functionality**
Currently, all generated man pages are placed in to a single-level directory: `<build-dir>/man`. Unfortunately, this cannot be used in combination with the unix `MANPATH` environment variable. The `man` program explicitly looks for man pages in section directories (such as `man/man1`, etc.). 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be great if sphinx would automatically create the section directories (e.g., `man/man1/`, `man/man3/`, etc.) and place each generated man page within appropriate section.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This problem can be over come within our project’s build system, ensuring the built man pages are installed in a correct location, but it would be nice if the build directory had the proper layout.

I’m happy to take a crack at implementing a fix, though this change in behavior may break some people who expect everything to appear in a `man/` directory.

261|        """Replace colons with hyphens in href and id attributes.

287|            if isinstance(next_node, nodes.Element):

293|    def add_visible_links(self, tree: nodes.document, show_urls: str = 'inline') -> None:
294|        """Add visible link targets for external links"""
295|
296|        def make_footnote_ref(doc: nodes.document, label: str) -> nodes.footnote_reference:
297|            """Create a footnote_reference node with children"""
298|            footnote_ref = nodes.footnote_reference('[#]_')
299|            footnote_ref.append(nodes.Text(label))
300|            doc.note_autofootnote_ref(footnote_ref)
301|            return footnote_ref
302|
303|        def make_footnote(doc: nodes.document, label: str, uri: str) -> nodes.footnote:
304|            """Create a footnote node with children"""
305|            footnote = nodes.footnote(uri)
306|            para = nodes.paragraph()
307|            para.append(nodes.Text(uri))
308|            footnote.append(para)
309|            footnote.insert(0, nodes.label('', label))
310|            doc.note_autofootnote(footnote)
311|            return footnote
312|
313|        def footnote_spot(tree: nodes.document) -> Tuple[Element, int]:
314|            """Find or create a spot to place footnotes.
315|
316|            The function returns the tuple (parent, index)."""
317|            # The code uses the following heuristic:
318|            # a) place them after the last existing footnote
319|            # b) place them after an (empty) Footnotes rubric
320|            # c) create an empty Footnotes rubric at the end of the document
321|            fns = tree.traverse(nodes.footnote)
322|            if fns:
323|                fn = fns[-1]
324|                return fn.parent, fn.parent.index(fn) + 1
325|            for node in tree.traverse(nodes.rubric):
326|                if len(node) == 1 and node.astext() == FOOTNOTES_RUBRIC_NAME:
327|                    return node.parent, node.parent.index(node) + 1
328|            doc = tree.traverse(nodes.document)[0]
329|            rub = nodes.rubric()
330|            rub.append(nodes.Text(FOOTNOTES_RUBRIC_NAME))
331|            doc.append(rub)
332|            return doc, doc.index(rub) + 1
333|
334|        if show_urls == 'no':
335|            return
336|        if show_urls == 'footnote':
337|            doc = tree.traverse(nodes.document)[0]
338|            fn_spot, fn_idx = footnote_spot(tree)
339|            nr = 1
340|        for node in tree.traverse(nodes.reference):
341|            uri = node.get('refuri', '')
342|            if (uri.startswith('http:') or uri.startswith('https:') or
343|                    uri.startswith('ftp:')) and uri not in node.astext():
344|                idx = node.parent.index(node) + 1
345|                if show_urls == 'inline':
346|                    uri = self.link_target_template % {'uri': uri}
347|                    link = nodes.inline(uri, uri)
348|                    link['classes'].append(self.css_link_target_class)
349|                    node.parent.insert(idx, link)
350|                elif show_urls == 'footnote':
351|                    label = FOOTNOTE_LABEL_TEMPLATE % nr
352|                    nr += 1
353|                    footnote_ref = make_footnote_ref(doc, label)
354|                    node.parent.insert(idx, footnote_ref)
355|                    footnote = make_footnote(doc, label, uri)
356|                    fn_spot.insert(fn_idx, footnote)
357|                    footnote_ref['refid'] = footnote['ids'][0]
358|                    footnote.add_backref(footnote_ref['ids'][0])
359|                    fn_idx += 1

394|    def copy_image_files_pil(self) -> None:
395|        """Copy images using Pillow, the Python Imaging Library.
396|        The method tries to read and write the files with Pillow, converting
397|        the format and resizing the image if necessary/possible.
398|        """
399|        ensuredir(path.join(self.outdir, self.imagedir))
400|        for src in status_iterator(self.images, __('copying images... '), "brown",
401|                                   len(self.images), self.app.verbosity):
402|            dest = self.images[src]
403|            try:
404|                img = Image.open(path.join(self.srcdir, src))
405|            except OSError:
406|                if not self.is_vector_graphics(src):
407|                    logger.warning(__('cannot read image file %r: copying it instead'),
408|                                   path.join(self.srcdir, src))
409|                try:
410|                    copyfile(path.join(self.srcdir, src),
411|                             path.join(self.outdir, self.imagedir, dest))
412|                except OSError as err:
413|                    logger.warning(__('cannot copy image file %r: %s'),
414|                                   path.join(self.srcdir, src), err)
415|                continue
416|            if self.config.epub_fix_images:
417|                if img.mode in ('P',):
418|                    # See the Pillow documentation for Image.convert()
419|                    # https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html#PIL.Image.Image.convert
420|                    img = img.convert()
421|            if self.config.epub_max_image_width > 0:
422|                (width, height) = img.size
423|                nw = self.config.epub_max_image_width
424|                if width > nw:
425|                    nh = (height * nw) / width
426|                    img = img.resize((nw, nh), Image.BICUBIC)
427|            try:
428|                img.save(path.join(self.outdir, self.imagedir, dest))
429|            except OSError as err:
430|                logger.warning(__('cannot write image file %r: %s'),
431|                               path.join(self.srcdir, src), err)

636|    def build_navpoints(self, nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[NavPoint]:
637|        """Create the toc navigation structure.
638|
639|        Subelements of a node are nested inside the navpoint.  For nested nodes
640|        the parent node is reinserted in the subnav.
641|        """
642|        navstack = []  # type: List[NavPoint]
643|        navstack.append(NavPoint('dummy', '', '', '', []))
644|        level = 0
645|        lastnode = None
646|        for node in nodes:
647|            if not node['text']:
648|                continue
649|            file = node['refuri'].split('#')[0]
650|            if file in self.ignored_files:
651|                continue
652|            if node['level'] > self.config.epub_tocdepth:
653|                continue
654|            if node['level'] == level:
655|                navpoint = self.new_navpoint(node, level)
656|                navstack.pop()
657|                navstack[-1].children.append(navpoint)
658|                navstack.append(navpoint)
659|            elif node['level'] == level + 1:
660|                level += 1
661|                if lastnode and self.config.epub_tocdup:
662|                    # Insert starting point in subtoc with same playOrder
663|                    navstack[-1].children.append(self.new_navpoint(lastnode, level, False))
664|                navpoint = self.new_navpoint(node, level)
665|                navstack[-1].children.append(navpoint)
666|                navstack.append(navpoint)
667|            elif node['level'] < level:
668|                while node['level'] < len(navstack):
669|                    navstack.pop()
670|                level = node['level']
671|                navpoint = self.new_navpoint(node, level)
672|                navstack[-1].children.append(navpoint)
673|                navstack.append(navpoint)
674|            else:
675|                raise
676|            lastnode = node
677|
678|        return navstack[0].children

354|def apart_list_full_decomposition(P, Q, dummygen):
355|    """
356|    Bronstein's full partial fraction decomposition algorithm.
357|
358|    Given a univariate rational function ``f``, performing only GCD
359|    operations over the algebraic closure of the initial ground domain
360|    of definition, compute full partial fraction decomposition with
361|    fractions having linear denominators.
362|
363|    Note that no factorization of the initial denominator of ``f`` is
364|    performed. The final decomposition is formed in terms of a sum of
365|    :class:`RootSum` instances.
366|
367|    References
368|    ==========
369|
370|    1. [Bronstein93]_
371|
372|    """
373|    f, x, U = P/Q, P.gen, []
374|
375|    u = Function('u')(x)
376|    a = Dummy('a')
377|
378|    partial = []
379|
380|    for d, n in Q.sqf_list_include(all=True):
381|        b = d.as_expr()
382|        U += [ u.diff(x, n - 1) ]
383|
384|        h = cancel(f*b**n) / u**n
385|
386|        H, subs = [h], []
387|
388|        for j in range(1, n):
389|            H += [ H[-1].diff(x) / j ]
390|
391|        for j in range(1, n + 1):
392|            subs += [ (U[j - 1], b.diff(x, j) / j) ]
393|
394|        for j in range(0, n):
395|            P, Q = cancel(H[j]).as_numer_denom()
396|
397|            for i in range(0, j + 1):
398|                P = P.subs(*subs[j - i])
399|
400|            Q = Q.subs(*subs[0])
401|
402|            P = Poly(P, x)
403|            Q = Poly(Q, x)
404|
405|            G = P.gcd(d)
406|            D = d.quo(G)
407|
408|            B, g = Q.half_gcdex(D)
409|            b = (P * B.quo(g)).rem(D)
410|
411|            Dw = D.subs(x, next(dummygen))
412|            numer = Lambda(a, b.as_expr().subs(x, a))
413|            denom = Lambda(a, (x - a))
414|            exponent = n-j
415|
416|            partial.append((Dw, numer, denom, exponent))
417|
418|    return partial

423|    r"""Reassemble a full partial fraction decomposition
424|    from a structured result obtained by the function ``apart_list``.
425|
426|    Examples
427|    ========
428|
429|    This example is taken from Bronstein's original paper:
430|
431|    >>> from sympy.polys.partfrac import apart_list, assemble_partfrac_list
432|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
433|
434|    >>> f = 36 / (x**5 - 2*x**4 - 2*x**3 + 4*x**2 + x - 2)
435|    >>> pfd = apart_list(f)
436|    >>> pfd
437|    (1,
438|    Poly(0, x, domain='ZZ'),
439|    [(Poly(_w - 2, _w, domain='ZZ'), Lambda(_a, 4), Lambda(_a, -_a + x), 1),
440|    (Poly(_w**2 - 1, _w, domain='ZZ'), Lambda(_a, -3*_a - 6), Lambda(_a, -_a + x), 2),
441|    (Poly(_w + 1, _w, domain='ZZ'), Lambda(_a, -4), Lambda(_a, -_a + x), 1)])
442|
443|    >>> assemble_partfrac_list(pfd)
444|    -4/(x + 1) - 3/(x + 1)**2 - 9/(x - 1)**2 + 4/(x - 2)
445|
446|    If we happen to know some roots we can provide them easily inside the structure:
447|
448|    >>> pfd = apart_list(2/(x**2-2))
449|    >>> pfd
450|    (1,
451|    Poly(0, x, domain='ZZ'),
452|    [(Poly(_w**2 - 2, _w, domain='ZZ'),
453|    Lambda(_a, _a/2),
454|    Lambda(_a, -_a + x),
455|    1)])
456|
457|    >>> pfda = assemble_partfrac_list(pfd)
458|    >>> pfda
459|    RootSum(_w**2 - 2, Lambda(_a, _a/(-_a + x)))/2
460|
461|    >>> pfda.doit()
462|    -sqrt(2)/(2*(x + sqrt(2))) + sqrt(2)/(2*(x - sqrt(2)))
463|
464|    >>> from sympy import Dummy, Poly, Lambda, sqrt
465|    >>> a = Dummy("a")
466|    >>> pfd = (1, Poly(0, x, domain='ZZ'), [([sqrt(2),-sqrt(2)], Lambda(a, a/2), Lambda(a, -a + x), 1)])
467|
468|    >>> assemble_partfrac_list(pfd)
469|    -sqrt(2)/(2*(x + sqrt(2))) + sqrt(2)/(2*(x - sqrt(2)))
470|
471|    See also
472|    ========
473|
474|    apart, apart_list
475|    """
476|    # Common factor
477|    common = partial_list[0]
478|
479|    # Polynomial part
480|    polypart = partial_list[1]
481|    pfd = polypart.as_expr()
482|
483|    # Rational parts
484|    for r, nf, df, ex in partial_list[2]:
485|        if isinstance(r, Poly):
486|            # Assemble in case the roots are given implicitly by a polynomials
487|            an, nu = nf.variables, nf.expr
488|            ad, de = df.variables, df.expr
489|            # Hack to make dummies equal because Lambda created new Dummies
490|            de = de.subs(ad[0], an[0])
491|            func = Lambda(an, nu/de**ex)
492|            pfd += RootSum(r, func, auto=False, quadratic=False)
493|        else:
494|            # Assemble in case the roots are given explicitely by a list of algebraic numbers
495|            for root in r:
496|                pfd += nf(root)/df(root)**ex

565|    def _print_Derivative(self, expr):
566|        dim = len(expr.variables)

569|        else:
570|            diff_symbol = r'd'
571|
572|
573|        if dim == 1:
574|            tex = r"\frac{%s}{%s %s}" % (diff_symbol, diff_symbol,
575|                self._print(expr.variables[0]))
576|        else:
577|            multiplicity, i, tex = [], 1, ""
578|            current = expr.variables[0]
579|
580|            for symbol in expr.variables[1:]:
581|                if symbol == current:
582|                    i = i + 1
583|                else:
584|                    multiplicity.append((current, i))
585|                    current, i = symbol, 1
586|            else:
587|                multiplicity.append((current, i))
588|
589|            for x, i in multiplicity:
590|                if i == 1:
591|                    tex += r"%s %s" % (diff_symbol, self._print(x))
592|                else:
593|                    tex += r"%s %s^{%s}" % (diff_symbol, self._print(x), i)
594|
595|            tex = r"\frac{%s^{%s}}{%s} " % (diff_symbol, dim, tex)
596|
597|        if isinstance(expr.expr, AssocOp):
598|            return r"%s\left(%s\right)" % (tex, self._print(expr.expr))
599|        else:
600|            return r"%s %s" % (tex, self._print(expr.expr))

657|    def _hprint_Function(self, func):
658|        '''
659|        Logic to decide how to render a function to latex
660|          - if it is a recognized latex name, use the appropriate latex command
661|          - if it is a single letter, just use that letter
662|          - if it is a longer name, then put \operatorname{} around it and be
663|            mindful of undercores in the name
664|        '''
665|        func = self._deal_with_super_sub(func)
666|
667|        if func in accepted_latex_functions:
668|            name = r"\%s" % func
669|        elif len(func) == 1 or func.startswith('\\'):
670|            name = func
671|        else:
672|            name = r"\operatorname{%s}" % func
673|        return name

675|    def _print_Function(self, expr, exp=None):
676|        '''
677|        Render functions to LaTeX, handling functions that LaTeX knows about
678|        e.g., sin, cos, ... by using the proper LaTeX command (\sin, \cos, ...).
679|        For single-letter function names, render them as regular LaTeX math
680|        symbols. For multi-letter function names that LaTeX does not know
681|        about, (e.g., Li, sech) use \operatorname{} so that the function name
682|        is rendered in Roman font and LaTeX handles spacing properly.
683|
684|        expr is the expression involving the function
685|        exp is an exponent
686|        '''
687|        func = expr.func.__name__
688|
689|        if hasattr(self, '_print_' + func):
690|            return getattr(self, '_print_' + func)(expr, exp)
691|        else:
692|            args = [ str(self._print(arg)) for arg in expr.args ]
693|            # How inverse trig functions should be displayed, formats are:
694|            # abbreviated: asin, full: arcsin, power: sin^-1
695|            inv_trig_style = self._settings['inv_trig_style']
696|            # If we are dealing with a power-style inverse trig function
697|            inv_trig_power_case = False
698|            # If it is applicable to fold the argument brackets
699|            can_fold_brackets = self._settings['fold_func_brackets'] and \
700|                len(args) == 1 and \
701|                not self._needs_function_brackets(expr.args[0])
702|
703|            inv_trig_table = ["asin", "acos", "atan", "acot"]
704|
705|            # If the function is an inverse trig function, handle the style
706|            if func in inv_trig_table:
707|                if inv_trig_style == "abbreviated":
708|                    func = func
709|                elif inv_trig_style == "full":
710|                    func = "arc" + func[1:]
711|                elif inv_trig_style == "power":
712|                    func = func[1:]
713|                    inv_trig_power_case = True
714|
715|                    # Can never fold brackets if we're raised to a power
716|                    if exp is not None:
717|                        can_fold_brackets = False
718|
719|            if inv_trig_power_case:
720|                if func in accepted_latex_functions:
721|                    name = r"\%s^{-1}" % func
722|                else:
723|                    name = r"\operatorname{%s}^{-1}" % func
724|            elif exp is not None:
725|                name = r'%s^{%s}' % (self._hprint_Function(func), exp)
726|            else:
727|                name = self._hprint_Function(func)
728|
729|            if can_fold_brackets:
730|                if func in accepted_latex_functions:
731|                    # Wrap argument safely to avoid parse-time conflicts
732|                    # with the function name itself
733|                    name += r" {%s}"
734|                else:
735|                    name += r"%s"
736|            else:
737|                name += r"{\left (%s \right )}"
738|
739|            if inv_trig_power_case and exp is not None:
740|                name += r"^{%s}" % exp
741|
742|            return name % ",".join(args)

595|    def _print_matrix_contents(self, e):
596|        """
597|        This method factors out what is essentially grid printing.
598|        """
599|        M = e   # matrix
600|        Ms = {}  # i,j -> pretty(M[i,j])
601|        for i in range(M.rows):
602|            for j in range(M.cols):
603|                Ms[i, j] = self._print(M[i, j])
604|
605|        # h- and v- spacers
606|        hsep = 2
607|        vsep = 1
608|
609|        # max width for columns
610|        maxw = [-1] * M.cols
611|
612|        for j in range(M.cols):
613|            maxw[j] = max([Ms[i, j].width() for i in range(M.rows)] or [0])
614|
615|        # drawing result
616|        D = None
617|
618|        for i in range(M.rows):
619|
620|            D_row = None
621|            for j in range(M.cols):
622|                s = Ms[i, j]
623|
624|                # reshape s to maxw
625|                # XXX this should be generalized, and go to stringPict.reshape ?
626|                assert s.width() <= maxw[j]
627|
628|                # hcenter it, +0.5 to the right                        2
629|                # ( it's better to align formula starts for say 0 and r )
630|                # XXX this is not good in all cases -- maybe introduce vbaseline?
631|                wdelta = maxw[j] - s.width()
632|                wleft = wdelta // 2
633|                wright = wdelta - wleft
634|
635|                s = prettyForm(*s.right(' '*wright))
636|                s = prettyForm(*s.left(' '*wleft))
637|
638|                # we don't need vcenter cells -- this is automatically done in
639|                # a pretty way because when their baselines are taking into
640|                # account in .right()
641|
642|                if D_row is None:
643|                    D_row = s   # first box in a row
644|                    continue
645|
646|                D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(' '*hsep))  # h-spacer
647|                D_row = prettyForm(*D_row.right(s))
648|
649|            if D is None:
650|                D = D_row       # first row in a picture
651|                continue
652|
653|            # v-spacer
654|            for _ in range(vsep):
655|                D = prettyForm(*D.below(' '))
656|
657|            D = prettyForm(*D.below(D_row))
658|
659|        if D is None:

661|
662|        return D

883|            even = True

893|                even = not even

1053|                s = prettyForm(*s.left(' ' * left))

1323|    def _print_Add(self, expr, order=None):

1328|        pforms, indices = [], []
1329|
1330|        def pretty_negative(pform, index):
1331|            """Prepend a minus sign to a pretty form. """
1332|            #TODO: Move this code to prettyForm
1333|            if index == 0:
1334|                if pform.height() > 1:
1335|                    pform_neg = '- '
1336|                else:
1337|                    pform_neg = '-'
1338|            else:
1339|                pform_neg = ' - '
1340|
1341|            if pform.binding > prettyForm.NEG:
1342|                p = stringPict(*pform.parens())
1343|            else:
1344|                p = pform
1345|            p = stringPict.next(pform_neg, p)
1346|            # Lower the binding to NEG, even if it was higher. Otherwise, it
1347|            # will print as a + ( - (b)), instead of a - (b).
1348|            return prettyForm(binding=prettyForm.NEG, *p)
1349|
1350|        for i, term in enumerate(terms):
1351|            if term.is_Mul and _coeff_isneg(term):
1352|                coeff, other = term.as_coeff_mul(rational=False)
1353|                pform = self._print(Mul(-coeff, *other, evaluate=False))
1354|                pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))

1357|                indices.append(i)

1360|                pforms.append(pretty_negative(pform, i))
1361|            elif term.is_Relational:
1362|                pforms.append(prettyForm(*self._print(term).parens()))
1363|            else:
1364|                pforms.append(self._print(term))
1365|
1366|        if indices:
1367|            large = True
1368|
1369|            for pform in pforms:
1370|                if pform is not None and pform.height() > 1:
1371|                    break
1372|            else:
1373|                large = False
1374|
1375|            for i in indices:
1376|                term, negative = terms[i], False
1377|
1378|                if term < 0:
1379|                    term, negative = -term, True
1380|
1381|                if large:

1383|                else:
1384|                    pform = self._print(term)
1385|
1386|                if negative:

1391|        return prettyForm.__add__(*pforms)

1420|        # is more than one term in the numer/denom

1423|                    isinstance(a[i], (Integral, Piecewise, Product, Sum))):

1425|            elif a[i].is_Relational:

1446|    def _print_nth_root(self, base, expt):
1447|        bpretty = self._print(base)
1448|
1449|        # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
1450|        if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
1451|            and expt is S.Half and bpretty.height() == 1
1452|            and (bpretty.width() == 1
1453|                 or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
1454|            return prettyForm(*bpretty.left(u'\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
1455|
1456|        # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
1457|        _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
1458|        rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
1459|        # Make exponent number to put above it
1460|        if isinstance(expt, Rational):
1461|            exp = str(expt.q)
1462|            if exp == '2':
1463|                exp = ''
1464|        else:
1465|            exp = str(expt.args[0])
1466|        exp = exp.ljust(2)
1467|        if len(exp) > 2:
1468|            rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
1469|        # Stack the exponent
1470|        rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
1471|        rootsign.baseline = 0
1472|        # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
1473|        linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
1474|        diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(
1475|            ' '*(linelength - i - 1) + _zZ + ' '*i
1476|            for i in range(linelength)
1477|        ))
1478|        # Put baseline just below lowest line: next to exp
1479|        diagonal.baseline = linelength - 1
1480|        # Make the root symbol
1481|        rootsign = prettyForm(*rootsign.right(diagonal))
1482|        # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height
1483|        # but if the height of bpretty is one, the rootsign must be one higher
1484|        rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
1485|        #build result
1486|        s = prettyForm(hobj('_', 2 + bpretty.width()))
1487|        s = prettyForm(*bpretty.above(s))
1488|        s = prettyForm(*s.left(rootsign))
1489|        return s

2403|    def dual(self):
2404|        """Returns the dual of a matrix, which is:
2405|
2406|        `(1/2)*levicivita(i, j, k, l)*M(k, l)` summed over indices `k` and `l`
2407|
2408|        Since the levicivita method is anti_symmetric for any pairwise
2409|        exchange of indices, the dual of a symmetric matrix is the zero
2410|        matrix. Strictly speaking the dual defined here assumes that the
2411|        'matrix' `M` is a contravariant anti_symmetric second rank tensor,
2412|        so that the dual is a covariant second rank tensor.
2413|
2414|        """
2415|        from sympy import LeviCivita
2416|        from sympy.matrices import zeros
2417|
2418|        M, n = self[:, :], self.rows
2419|        work = zeros(n)
2420|        if self.is_symmetric():
2421|            return work
2422|
2423|        for i in range(1, n):
2424|            for j in range(1, n):
2425|                acum = 0
2426|                for k in range(1, n):
2427|                    acum += LeviCivita(i, j, 0, k) * M[0, k]
2428|                work[i, j] = acum
2429|                work[j, i] = -acum
2430|
2431|        for l in range(1, n):
2432|            acum = 0
2433|            for a in range(1, n):
2434|                for b in range(1, n):
2435|                    acum += LeviCivita(0, l, a, b) * M[a, b]
2436|            acum /= 2
2437|            work[0, l] = -acum
2438|            work[l, 0] = acum
2439|
2440|        return work

2442|    def exp(self):
2443|        """Return the exponentiation of a square matrix."""
2444|        if not self.is_square:
2445|            raise NonSquareMatrixError(
2446|                "Exponentiation is valid only for square matrices")
2447|        try:
2448|            P, J = self.jordan_form()
2449|            cells = J.get_diag_blocks()
2450|        except MatrixError:
2451|            raise NotImplementedError(
2452|                "Exponentiation is implemented only for matrices for which the Jordan normal form can be computed")
2453|
2454|        def _jblock_exponential(b):
2455|            # This function computes the matrix exponential for one single Jordan block
2456|            nr = b.rows
2457|            l = b[0, 0]
2458|            if nr == 1:
2459|                res = exp(l)
2460|            else:
2461|                from sympy import eye
2462|                # extract the diagonal part
2463|                d = b[0, 0] * eye(nr)
2464|                # and the nilpotent part
2465|                n = b - d
2466|                # compute its exponential
2467|                nex = eye(nr)
2468|                for i in range(1, nr):
2469|                    nex = nex + n ** i / factorial(i)
2470|                # combine the two parts
2471|                res = exp(b[0, 0]) * nex
2472|            return (res)
2473|
2474|        blocks = list(map(_jblock_exponential, cells))
2475|        from sympy.matrices import diag
2476|        eJ = diag(*blocks)
2477|        # n = self.rows
2478|        ret = P * eJ * P.inv()
2479|        return type(self)(ret)

2538|        >>> sol
2539|        Matrix([
2540|        [-1],
2541|        [ 2],
2542|        [ 0]])
2543|        >>> params
2544|        Matrix(0, 1, [])
2545|
2546|        See Also
2547|        ========
2548|
2549|        lower_triangular_solve
2550|        upper_triangular_solve
2551|        cholesky_solve
2552|        diagonal_solve
2553|        LDLsolve
2554|        LUsolve
2555|        QRsolve
2556|        pinv
2557|
2558|        References
2559|        ==========
2560|
2561|        .. [1] http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaussian_elimination
2562|
2563|        """
2564|        from sympy.matrices import Matrix, zeros
2565|
2566|        aug = self.hstack(self.copy(), b.copy())
2567|        row, col = aug[:, :-1].shape
2568|
2569|        # solve by reduced row echelon form
2570|        A, pivots = aug.rref(simplify=True)
2571|        A, v = A[:, :-1], A[:, -1]
2572|        pivots = list(filter(lambda p: p < col, pivots))
2573|        rank = len(pivots)
2574|
2575|        # Bring to block form
2576|        permutation = Matrix(range(col)).T
2577|        A = A.vstack(A, permutation)
2578|
2579|        for i, c in enumerate(pivots):
2580|            A.col_swap(i, c)
2581|
2582|        A, permutation = A[:-1, :], A[-1, :]
2583|
2584|        # check for existence of solutions
2585|        # rank of aug Matrix should be equal to rank of coefficient matrix
2586|        if not v[rank:, 0].is_zero:
2587|            raise ValueError("Linear system has no solution")
2588|
2589|        # Get index of free symbols (free parameters)
2590|        free_var_index = permutation[
2591|                         len(pivots):]  # non-pivots columns are free variables
2592|
2593|        # Free parameters
2594|        dummygen = numbered_symbols("tau", Dummy)
2595|        tau = Matrix([next(dummygen) for k in range(col - rank)]).reshape(
2596|            col - rank, 1)
2597|
2598|        # Full parametric solution
2599|        V = A[:rank, rank:]
2600|        vt = v[:rank, 0]
2601|        free_sol = tau.vstack(vt - V * tau, tau)
2602|
2603|        # Undo permutation
2604|        sol = zeros(col, 1)
2605|        for k, v in enumerate(free_sol):
2606|            sol[permutation[k], 0] = v
2607|
2608|        if freevar:
2609|            return sol, tau, free_var_index
2610|        else:
2611|            return sol, tau

2613|    def inv_mod(self, m):
2614|        r"""
2615|        Returns the inverse of the matrix `K` (mod `m`), if it exists.
2616|
2617|        Method to find the matrix inverse of `K` (mod `m`) implemented in this function:
2618|
2619|        * Compute `\mathrm{adj}(K) = \mathrm{cof}(K)^t`, the adjoint matrix of `K`.
2620|
2621|        * Compute `r = 1/\mathrm{det}(K) \pmod m`.
2622|
2623|        * `K^{-1} = r\cdot \mathrm{adj}(K) \pmod m`.
2624|
2625|        Examples
2626|        ========
2627|
2628|        >>> from sympy import Matrix
2629|        >>> A = Matrix(2, 2, [1, 2, 3, 4])
2630|        >>> A.inv_mod(5)
2631|        Matrix([
2632|        [3, 1],
2633|        [4, 2]])
2634|        >>> A.inv_mod(3)
2635|        Matrix([
2636|        [1, 1],
2637|        [0, 1]])
2638|
2639|        """
2640|        from sympy.ntheory import totient
2641|        if not self.is_square:
2642|            raise NonSquareMatrixError()
2643|        N = self.cols
2644|        phi = totient(m)
2645|        det_K = self.det()
2646|        if gcd(det_K, m) != 1:
2647|            raise ValueError('Matrix is not invertible (mod %d)' % m)
2648|        det_inv = pow(int(det_K), int(phi - 1), int(m))
2649|        K_adj = self.adjugate()
2650|        K_inv = self.__class__(N, N,
2651|                               [det_inv * K_adj[i, j] % m for i in range(N) for
2652|                                j in range(N)])
2653|        return K_inv

2655|    def inverse_ADJ(self, iszerofunc=_iszero):
2656|        """Calculates the inverse using the adjugate matrix and a determinant.
2657|
2658|        See Also
2659|        ========
2660|
2661|        inv
2662|        inverse_LU
2663|        inverse_GE
2664|        """
2665|        if not self.is_square:
2666|            raise NonSquareMatrixError("A Matrix must be square to invert.")
2667|
2668|        d = self.det(method='berkowitz')
2669|        zero = d.equals(0)
2670|        if zero is None:
2671|            # if equals() can't decide, will rref be able to?
2672|            ok = self.rref(simplify=True)[0]
2673|            zero = any(iszerofunc(ok[j, j]) for j in range(ok.rows))
2674|        if zero:
2675|            raise ValueError("Matrix det == 0; not invertible.")
2676|
2677|        return self.adjugate() / d

2692|
2693|        big = Matrix.hstack(self.as_mutable(), Matrix.eye(self.rows))
2694|        red = big.rref(iszerofunc=iszerofunc, simplify=True)[0]

2787|        a zero matrix.

2811|    def key2bounds(self, keys):
2812|        """Converts a key with potentially mixed types of keys (integer and slice)
2813|        into a tuple of ranges and raises an error if any index is out of self's
2814|        range.

2826|            else:
2827|                rlo, rhi = keys[0].indices(self.rows)[:2]
2828|        else:
2829|            rlo = a2idx(keys[0], self.rows)
2830|            rhi = rlo + 1
2831|        if jslice:

2834|            else:
2835|                clo, chi = keys[1].indices(self.cols)[:2]

2841|    def key2ij(self, key):
2842|        """Converts key into canonical form, converting integers or indexable
2843|        items into valid integers for self's range or returning slices
2844|        unchanged.

2854|            return [a2idx(i, n) if not isinstance(i, slice) else i

2880|        >>> D

2882|        [25, 0, 0],
2883|        [ 0, 9, 0],

2901|    def LDLsolve(self, rhs):
2902|        """Solves Ax = B using LDL decomposition,
2903|        for a general square and non-singular matrix.
2904|
2905|        For a non-square matrix with rows > cols,
2906|        the least squares solution is returned.

2909|        ========

2912|        >>> A = eye(2)*2
2913|        >>> B = Matrix([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
2914|        >>> A.LDLsolve(B) == B/2

2918|        ========

2921|        lower_triangular_solve
2922|        upper_triangular_solve
2923|        gauss_jordan_solve
2924|        cholesky_solve
2925|        diagonal_solve
2926|        LUsolve
2927|        QRsolve
2928|        pinv_solve

2930|        if self.is_symmetric():
2931|            L, D = self.LDLdecomposition()
2932|        elif self.rows >= self.cols:

2934|            rhs = self.T * rhs

2966|    def LUdecomposition(self,
2967|                        iszerofunc=_iszero,
2968|                        simpfunc=None,
2969|                        rankcheck=False):
2970|        """Returns (L, U, perm) where L is a lower triangular matrix with unit
2971|        diagonal, U is an upper triangular matrix, and perm is a list of row
2972|        swap index pairs. If A is the original matrix, then
2973|        A = (L*U).permuteBkwd(perm), and the row permutation matrix P such
2974|        that P*A = L*U can be computed by P=eye(A.row).permuteFwd(perm).
2975|
2976|        See documentation for LUCombined for details about the keyword argument
2977|        rankcheck, iszerofunc, and simpfunc.
2978|
2979|        Examples
2980|        ========
2981|
2982|        >>> from sympy import Matrix
2983|        >>> a = Matrix([[4, 3], [6, 3]])
2984|        >>> L, U, _ = a.LUdecomposition()
2985|        >>> L
2986|        Matrix([
2987|        [  1, 0],
2988|        [3/2, 1]])
2989|        >>> U
2990|        Matrix([
2991|        [4,    3],
2992|        [0, -3/2]])
2993|
2994|        See Also
2995|        ========
2996|
2997|        cholesky
2998|        LDLdecomposition
2999|        QRdecomposition
3000|        LUdecomposition_Simple
3001|        LUdecompositionFF
3002|        LUsolve
3003|        """
3004|
3005|        combined, p = self.LUdecomposition_Simple(iszerofunc=iszerofunc,
3006|                                                  simpfunc=simpfunc,
3007|                                                  rankcheck=rankcheck)
3008|
3009|        # L is lower triangular self.rows x self.rows
3010|        # U is upper triangular self.rows x self.cols
3011|        # L has unit diagonal. For each column in combined, the subcolumn
3012|        # below the diagonal of combined is shared by L.
3013|        # If L has more columns than combined, then the remaining subcolumns
3014|        # below the diagonal of L are zero.
3015|        # The upper triangular portion of L and combined are equal.
3016|        def entry_L(i, j):
3017|            if i < j:
3018|                # Super diagonal entry
3019|                return S.Zero
3020|            elif i == j:
3021|                return S.One
3022|            elif j < combined.cols:
3023|                return combined[i, j]
3024|            # Subdiagonal entry of L with no corresponding
3025|            # entry in combined
3026|            return S.Zero
3027|
3028|        def entry_U(i, j):
3029|            return S.Zero if i > j else combined[i, j]
3030|
3031|        L = self._new(combined.rows, combined.rows, entry_L)
3032|        U = self._new(combined.rows, combined.cols, entry_U)
3033|
3034|        return L, U, p

3037|    def LUdecomposition_Simple(self,
3038|                               iszerofunc=_iszero,
3039|                               simpfunc=None,
3040|                               rankcheck=False):
3041|        """Compute an lu decomposition of m x n matrix A, where P*A = L*U
3042|
3043|        * L is m x m lower triangular with unit diagonal
3044|        * U is m x n upper triangular
3045|        * P is an m x m permutation matrix
3046|
3047|        Returns an m x n matrix lu, and an m element list perm where each
3048|        element of perm is a pair of row exchange indices.
3049|
3050|        The factors L and U are stored in lu as follows:
3051|        The subdiagonal elements of L are stored in the subdiagonal elements
3052|        of lu, that is lu[i, j] = L[i, j] whenever i > j.
3053|        The elements on the diagonal of L are all 1, and are not explicitly
3054|        stored.
3055|        U is stored in the upper triangular portion of lu, that is
3056|        lu[i ,j] = U[i, j] whenever i <= j.
3057|        The output matrix can be visualized as:
3058|
3059|        Matrix([
3060|            [u, u, u, u],
3061|            [l, u, u, u],
3062|            [l, l, u, u],
3063|            [l, l, l, u]])
3064|
3065|        where l represents a subdiagonal entry of the L factor, and u
3066|        represents an entry from the upper triangular entry of the U
3067|        factor.
3068|
3069|        perm is a list row swap index pairs such that if A is the original
3070|        matrix, then A = (L*U).permuteBkwd(perm), and the row permutation
3071|        matrix P such that P*A = L*U can be computed by
3072|        soP=eye(A.row).permuteFwd(perm).
3073|
3074|        The keyword argument rankcheck determines if this function raises a
3075|        ValueError when passed a matrix whose rank is strictly less than
3076|        min(num rows, num cols). The default behavior is to decompose a rank
3077|        deficient matrix. Pass rankcheck=True to raise a
3078|        ValueError instead. (This mimics the previous behavior of this function).
3079|
3080|        The keyword arguments iszerofunc and simpfunc are used by the pivot
3081|        search algorithm.
3082|        iszerofunc is a callable that returns a boolean indicating if its
3083|        input is zero, or None if it cannot make the determination.
3084|        simpfunc is a callable that simplifies its input.
3085|        The default is simpfunc=None, which indicate that the pivot search
3086|        algorithm should not attempt to simplify any candidate pivots.
3087|        If simpfunc fails to simplify its input, then it must return its input
3088|        instead of a copy.
3089|
3090|        When a matrix contains symbolic entries, the pivot search algorithm
3091|        differs from the case where every entry can be categorized as zero or
3092|        nonzero.
3093|        The algorithm searches column by column through the submatrix whose
3094|        top left entry coincides with the pivot position.
3095|        If it exists, the pivot is the first entry in the current search
3096|        column that iszerofunc guarantees is nonzero.
3097|        If no such candidate exists, then each candidate pivot is simplified
3098|        if simpfunc is not None.
3099|        The search is repeated, with the difference that a candidate may be
3100|        the pivot if `iszerofunc()` cannot guarantee that it is nonzero.
3101|        In the second search the pivot is the first candidate that
3102|        iszerofunc can guarantee is nonzero.
3103|        If no such candidate exists, then the pivot is the first candidate
3104|        for which iszerofunc returns None.
3105|        If no such candidate exists, then the search is repeated in the next
3106|        column to the right.
3107|        The pivot search algorithm differs from the one in `rref()`, which
3108|        relies on `_find_reasonable_pivot()`.
3109|        Future versions of `LUdecomposition_simple()` may use
3110|        `_find_reasonable_pivot()`.
3111|
3112|        See Also
3113|        ========
3114|
3115|        LUdecomposition
3116|        LUdecompositionFF
3117|        LUsolve
3118|        """
3119|
3120|        if rankcheck:
3121|            # https://github.com/sympy/sympy/issues/9796
3122|            pass
3123|
3124|        if self.rows == 0 or self.cols == 0:
3125|            # Define LU decomposition of a matrix with no entries as a matrix
3126|            # of the same dimensions with all zero entries.
3127|            return self.zeros(self.rows, self.cols), []
3128|
3129|        lu = self.as_mutable()
3130|        row_swaps = []
3131|
3132|        pivot_col = 0
3133|        for pivot_row in range(0, lu.rows - 1):
3134|            # Search for pivot. Prefer entry that iszeropivot determines
3135|            # is nonzero, over entry that iszeropivot cannot guarantee
3136|            # is  zero.
3137|            # XXX `_find_reasonable_pivot` uses slow zero testing. Blocked by bug #10279
3138|            # Future versions of LUdecomposition_simple can pass iszerofunc and simpfunc
3139|            # to _find_reasonable_pivot().
3140|            # In pass 3 of _find_reasonable_pivot(), the predicate in `if x.equals(S.Zero):`
3141|            # calls sympy.simplify(), and not the simplification function passed in via
3142|            # the keyword argument simpfunc.
3143|
3144|            iszeropivot = True
3145|            while pivot_col != self.cols and iszeropivot:
3146|                sub_col = (lu[r, pivot_col] for r in range(pivot_row, self.rows))
3147|                pivot_row_offset, pivot_value, is_assumed_non_zero, ind_simplified_pairs =\
3148|                    _find_reasonable_pivot_naive(sub_col, iszerofunc, simpfunc)
3149|                iszeropivot = pivot_value is None
3150|                if iszeropivot:
3151|                    # All candidate pivots in this column are zero.
3152|                    # Proceed to next column.
3153|                    pivot_col += 1
3154|
3155|            if rankcheck and pivot_col != pivot_row:
3156|                # All entries including and below the pivot position are
3157|                # zero, which indicates that the rank of the matrix is
3158|                # strictly less than min(num rows, num cols)
3159|                # Mimic behavior of previous implementation, by throwing a
3160|                # ValueError.
3161|                raise ValueError("Rank of matrix is strictly less than"
3162|                                 " number of rows or columns."
3163|                                 " Pass keyword argument"
3164|                                 " rankcheck=False to compute"
3165|                                 " the LU decomposition of this matrix.")
3166|
3167|            candidate_pivot_row = None if pivot_row_offset is None else pivot_row + pivot_row_offset
3168|
3169|            if candidate_pivot_row is None and iszeropivot:
3170|                # If candidate_pivot_row is None and iszeropivot is True
3171|                # after pivot search has completed, then the submatrix
3172|                # below and to the right of (pivot_row, pivot_col) is
3173|                # all zeros, indicating that Gaussian elimination is
3174|                # complete.
3175|                return lu, row_swaps
3176|
3177|            # Update entries simplified during pivot search.
3178|            for offset, val in ind_simplified_pairs:
3179|                lu[pivot_row + offset, pivot_col] = val
3180|
3181|            if pivot_row != candidate_pivot_row:
3182|                # Row swap book keeping:
3183|                # Record which rows were swapped.
3184|                # Update stored portion of L factor by multiplying L on the
3185|                # left and right with the current permutation.
3186|                # Swap rows of U.
3187|                row_swaps.append([pivot_row, candidate_pivot_row])
3188|
3189|                # Update L.
3190|                lu[pivot_row, 0:pivot_row], lu[candidate_pivot_row, 0:pivot_row] = \
3191|                    lu[candidate_pivot_row, 0:pivot_row], lu[pivot_row, 0:pivot_row]
3192|
3193|                # Swap pivot row of U with candidate pivot row.
3194|                lu[pivot_row, pivot_col:lu.cols], lu[candidate_pivot_row, pivot_col:lu.cols] = \
3195|                    lu[candidate_pivot_row, pivot_col:lu.cols], lu[pivot_row, pivot_col:lu.cols]
3196|
3197|            # Introduce zeros below the pivot by adding a multiple of the
3198|            # pivot row to a row under it, and store the result in the
3199|            # row under it.
3200|            # Only entries in the target row whose index is greater than
3201|            # start_col may be nonzero.
3202|            start_col = pivot_col + 1
3203|            for row in range(pivot_row + 1, lu.rows):
3204|                # Store factors of L in the subcolumn below
3205|                # (pivot_row, pivot_row).
3206|                lu[row, pivot_row] =\
3207|                    lu[row, pivot_col]/lu[pivot_row, pivot_col]
3208|
3209|                # Form the linear combination of the pivot row and the current
3210|                # row below the pivot row that zeros the entries below the pivot.
3211|                # Employing slicing instead of a loop here raises
3212|                # NotImplementedError: Cannot add Zero to MutableSparseMatrix
3213|                # in sympy/matrices/tests/test_sparse.py.
3214|                # c = pivot_row + 1 if pivot_row == pivot_col else pivot_col
3215|                for c in range(start_col, lu.cols):
3216|                    lu[row, c] = lu[row, c] - lu[row, pivot_row]*lu[pivot_row, c]
3217|
3218|            if pivot_row != pivot_col:
3219|                # matrix rank < min(num rows, num cols),
3220|                # so factors of L are not stored directly below the pivot.
3221|                # These entries are zero by construction, so don't bother
3222|                # computing them.
3223|                for row in range(pivot_row + 1, lu.rows):
3224|                    lu[row, pivot_col] = S.Zero
3225|
3226|            pivot_col += 1
3227|            if pivot_col == lu.cols:
3228|                # All candidate pivots are zero implies that Gaussian
3229|                # elimination is complete.
3230|                return lu, row_swaps
3231|
3232|        return lu, row_swaps

3234|    def LUdecompositionFF(self):
3235|        """Compute a fraction-free LU decomposition.
3236|
3237|        Returns 4 matrices P, L, D, U such that PA = L D**-1 U.
3238|        If the elements of the matrix belong to some integral domain I, then all
3239|        elements of L, D and U are guaranteed to belong to I.
3240|
3241|        **Reference**
3242|            - W. Zhou & D.J. Jeffrey, "Fraction-free matrix factors: new forms
3243|              for LU and QR factors". Frontiers in Computer Science in China,
3244|              Vol 2, no. 1, pp. 67-80, 2008.
3245|
3246|        See Also
3247|        ========
3248|
3249|        LUdecomposition
3250|        LUdecomposition_Simple
3251|        LUsolve
3252|        """
3253|        from sympy.matrices import SparseMatrix
3254|        zeros = SparseMatrix.zeros
3255|        eye = SparseMatrix.eye
3256|
3257|        n, m = self.rows, self.cols
3258|        U, L, P = self.as_mutable(), eye(n), eye(n)
3259|        DD = zeros(n, n)
3260|        oldpivot = 1
3261|
3262|        for k in range(n - 1):
3263|            if U[k, k] == 0:
3264|                for kpivot in range(k + 1, n):
3265|                    if U[kpivot, k]:
3266|                        break
3267|                else:
3268|                    raise ValueError("Matrix is not full rank")
3269|                U[k, k:], U[kpivot, k:] = U[kpivot, k:], U[k, k:]
3270|                L[k, :k], L[kpivot, :k] = L[kpivot, :k], L[k, :k]
3271|                P[k, :], P[kpivot, :] = P[kpivot, :], P[k, :]
3272|            L[k, k] = Ukk = U[k, k]
3273|            DD[k, k] = oldpivot * Ukk
3274|            for i in range(k + 1, n):
3275|                L[i, k] = Uik = U[i, k]
3276|                for j in range(k + 1, m):
3277|                    U[i, j] = (Ukk * U[i, j] - U[k, j] * Uik) / oldpivot
3278|                U[i, k] = 0
3279|            oldpivot = Ukk
3280|        DD[n - 1, n - 1] = oldpivot
3281|        return P, L, DD, U
3282|
3283|    def LUsolve(self, rhs, iszerofunc=_iszero):
3284|        """Solve the linear system Ax = rhs for x where A = self.
3285|
3286|        This is for symbolic matrices, for real or complex ones use
3287|        mpmath.lu_solve or mpmath.qr_solve.
3288|
3289|        See Also
3290|        ========
3291|
3292|        lower_triangular_solve
3293|        upper_triangular_solve
3294|        gauss_jordan_solve
3295|        cholesky_solve
3296|        diagonal_solve
3297|        LDLsolve
3298|        QRsolve
3299|        pinv_solve
3300|        LUdecomposition
3301|        """
3302|        if rhs.rows != self.rows:
3303|            raise ShapeError(
3304|                "`self` and `rhs` must have the same number of rows.")
3305|
3306|        A, perm = self.LUdecomposition_Simple(iszerofunc=_iszero)
3307|        n = self.rows
3308|        b = rhs.permute_rows(perm).as_mutable()
3309|        # forward substitution, all diag entries are scaled to 1
3310|        for i in range(n):
3311|            for j in range(i):
3312|                scale = A[i, j]
3313|                b.zip_row_op(i, j, lambda x, y: x - y * scale)
3314|        # backward substitution
3315|        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
3316|            for j in range(i + 1, n):
3317|                scale = A[i, j]
3318|                b.zip_row_op(i, j, lambda x, y: x - y * scale)
3319|            scale = A[i, i]
3320|            b.row_op(i, lambda x, _: x / scale)
3321|        return rhs.__class__(b)

3349|    def norm(self, ord=None):
3350|        """Return the Norm of a Matrix or Vector.
3351|        In the simplest case this is the geometric size of the vector
3352|        Other norms can be specified by the ord parameter
3353|
3354|
3355|        =====  ============================  ==========================
3356|        ord    norm for matrices             norm for vectors
3357|        =====  ============================  ==========================
3358|        None   Frobenius norm                2-norm
3359|        'fro'  Frobenius norm                - does not exist
3360|        inf    --                            max(abs(x))
3361|        -inf   --                            min(abs(x))
3362|        1      --                            as below
3363|        -1     --                            as below
3364|        2      2-norm (largest sing. value)  as below
3365|        -2     smallest singular value       as below
3366|        other  - does not exist              sum(abs(x)**ord)**(1./ord)
3367|        =====  ============================  ==========================
3368|
3369|        Examples
3370|        ========
3371|
3372|        >>> from sympy import Matrix, Symbol, trigsimp, cos, sin, oo
3373|        >>> x = Symbol('x', real=True)
3374|        >>> v = Matrix([cos(x), sin(x)])
3375|        >>> trigsimp( v.norm() )
3376|        1
3377|        >>> v.norm(10)
3378|        (sin(x)**10 + cos(x)**10)**(1/10)
3379|        >>> A = Matrix([[1, 1], [1, 1]])
3380|        >>> A.norm(2)# Spectral norm (max of |Ax|/|x| under 2-vector-norm)
3381|        2
3382|        >>> A.norm(-2) # Inverse spectral norm (smallest singular value)
3383|        0
3384|        >>> A.norm() # Frobenius Norm
3385|        2
3386|        >>> Matrix([1, -2]).norm(oo)
3387|        2
3388|        >>> Matrix([-1, 2]).norm(-oo)
3389|        1
3390|
3391|        See Also
3392|        ========
3393|
3394|        normalized
3395|        """
3396|        # Row or Column Vector Norms
3397|        vals = list(self.values()) or [0]
3398|        if self.rows == 1 or self.cols == 1:
3399|            if ord == 2 or ord is None:  # Common case sqrt(<x, x>)
3400|                return sqrt(Add(*(abs(i) ** 2 for i in vals)))
3401|
3402|            elif ord == 1:  # sum(abs(x))
3403|                return Add(*(abs(i) for i in vals))
3404|
3405|            elif ord == S.Infinity:  # max(abs(x))
3406|                return Max(*[abs(i) for i in vals])
3407|
3408|            elif ord == S.NegativeInfinity:  # min(abs(x))
3409|                return Min(*[abs(i) for i in vals])
3410|
3411|            # Otherwise generalize the 2-norm, Sum(x_i**ord)**(1/ord)
3412|            # Note that while useful this is not mathematically a norm
3413|            try:
3414|                return Pow(Add(*(abs(i) ** ord for i in vals)), S(1) / ord)
3415|            except (NotImplementedError, TypeError):
3416|                raise ValueError("Expected order to be Number, Symbol, oo")
3417|
3418|        # Matrix Norms
3419|        else:
3420|            if ord == 2:  # Spectral Norm
3421|                # Maximum singular value
3422|                return Max(*self.singular_values())
3423|
3424|            elif ord == -2:
3425|                # Minimum singular value
3426|                return Min(*self.singular_values())
3427|
3428|            elif (ord is None or isinstance(ord,
3429|                                            string_types) and ord.lower() in
3430|                ['f', 'fro', 'frobenius', 'vector']):
3431|                # Reshape as vector and send back to norm function
3432|                return self.vec().norm(ord=2)
3433|
3434|            else:
3435|                raise NotImplementedError("Matrix Norms under development")

3437|    def pinv_solve(self, B, arbitrary_matrix=None):
3438|        """Solve Ax = B using the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.
3439|
3440|        There may be zero, one, or infinite solutions.  If one solution
3441|        exists, it will be returned.  If infinite solutions exist, one will
3442|        be returned based on the value of arbitrary_matrix.  If no solutions
3443|        exist, the least-squares solution is returned.
3444|
3445|        Parameters
3446|        ==========
3447|
3448|        B : Matrix
3449|            The right hand side of the equation to be solved for.  Must have
3450|            the same number of rows as matrix A.
3451|        arbitrary_matrix : Matrix
3452|            If the system is underdetermined (e.g. A has more columns than
3453|            rows), infinite solutions are possible, in terms of an arbitrary
3454|            matrix.  This parameter may be set to a specific matrix to use
3455|            for that purpose; if so, it must be the same shape as x, with as
3456|            many rows as matrix A has columns, and as many columns as matrix
3457|            B.  If left as None, an appropriate matrix containing dummy
3458|            symbols in the form of ``wn_m`` will be used, with n and m being
3459|            row and column position of each symbol.
3460|
3461|        Returns
3462|        =======
3463|
3464|        x : Matrix
3465|            The matrix that will satisfy Ax = B.  Will have as many rows as
3466|            matrix A has columns, and as many columns as matrix B.
3467|
3468|        Examples
3469|        ========
3470|
3471|        >>> from sympy import Matrix
3472|        >>> A = Matrix([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
3473|        >>> B = Matrix([7, 8])
3474|        >>> A.pinv_solve(B)
3475|        Matrix([
3476|        [ _w0_0/6 - _w1_0/3 + _w2_0/6 - 55/18],
3477|        [-_w0_0/3 + 2*_w1_0/3 - _w2_0/3 + 1/9],
3478|        [ _w0_0/6 - _w1_0/3 + _w2_0/6 + 59/18]])
3479|        >>> A.pinv_solve(B, arbitrary_matrix=Matrix([0, 0, 0]))
3480|        Matrix([
3481|        [-55/18],
3482|        [   1/9],
3483|        [ 59/18]])
3484|
3485|        See Also
3486|        ========
3487|
3488|        lower_triangular_solve
3489|        upper_triangular_solve
3490|        gauss_jordan_solve
3491|        cholesky_solve
3492|        diagonal_solve
3493|        LDLsolve
3494|        LUsolve
3495|        QRsolve
3496|        pinv
3497|
3498|        Notes
3499|        =====
3500|
3501|        This may return either exact solutions or least squares solutions.
3502|        To determine which, check ``A * A.pinv() * B == B``.  It will be
3503|        True if exact solutions exist, and False if only a least-squares
3504|        solution exists.  Be aware that the left hand side of that equation
3505|        may need to be simplified to correctly compare to the right hand
3506|        side.
3507|
3508|        References
3509|        ==========
3510|
3511|        .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moore-Penrose_pseudoinverse#Obtaining_all_solutions_of_a_linear_system
3512|
3513|        """
3514|        from sympy.matrices import eye
3515|        A = self
3516|        A_pinv = self.pinv()
3517|        if arbitrary_matrix is None:
3518|            rows, cols = A.cols, B.cols
3519|            w = symbols('w:{0}_:{1}'.format(rows, cols), cls=Dummy)
3520|            arbitrary_matrix = self.__class__(cols, rows, w).T
3521|        return A_pinv * B + (eye(A.cols) - A_pinv * A) * arbitrary_matrix
3522|
3523|    def pinv(self):
3524|        """Calculate the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the matrix.
3525|
3526|        The Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse exists and is unique for any matrix.
3527|        If the matrix is invertible, the pseudoinverse is the same as the
3528|        inverse.
3529|
3530|        Examples
3531|        ========
3532|
3533|        >>> from sympy import Matrix
3534|        >>> Matrix([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]).pinv()
3535|        Matrix([
3536|        [-17/18,  4/9],
3537|        [  -1/9,  1/9],
3538|        [ 13/18, -2/9]])
3539|
3540|        See Also
3541|        ========
3542|
3543|        inv
3544|        pinv_solve
3545|
3546|        References
3547|        ==========
3548|
3549|        .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moore-Penrose_pseudoinverse
3550|
3551|        """
3552|        A = self
3553|        AH = self.H
3554|        # Trivial case: pseudoinverse of all-zero matrix is its transpose.
3555|        if A.is_zero:
3556|            return AH
3557|        try:
3558|            if self.rows >= self.cols:
3559|                return (AH * A).inv() * AH
3560|            else:
3561|                return AH * (A * AH).inv()
3562|        except ValueError:
3563|            # Matrix is not full rank, so A*AH cannot be inverted.
3564|            raise NotImplementedError('Rank-deficient matrices are not yet '
3565|                                      'supported.')

3617|    def QRdecomposition(self):
3618|        """Return Q, R where A = Q*R, Q is orthogonal and R is upper triangular.
3619|
3620|        Examples
3621|        ========
3622|
3623|        This is the example from wikipedia:
3624|
3625|        >>> from sympy import Matrix
3626|        >>> A = Matrix([[12, -51, 4], [6, 167, -68], [-4, 24, -41]])
3627|        >>> Q, R = A.QRdecomposition()
3628|        >>> Q
3629|        Matrix([
3630|        [ 6/7, -69/175, -58/175],
3631|        [ 3/7, 158/175,   6/175],
3632|        [-2/7,    6/35,  -33/35]])
3633|        >>> R
3634|        Matrix([
3635|        [14,  21, -14],
3636|        [ 0, 175, -70],
3637|        [ 0,   0,  35]])
3638|        >>> A == Q*R
3639|        True
3640|
3641|        QR factorization of an identity matrix:
3642|
3643|        >>> A = Matrix([[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]])
3644|        >>> Q, R = A.QRdecomposition()
3645|        >>> Q
3646|        Matrix([
3647|        [1, 0, 0],
3648|        [0, 1, 0],
3649|        [0, 0, 1]])
3650|        >>> R
3651|        Matrix([
3652|        [1, 0, 0],
3653|        [0, 1, 0],
3654|        [0, 0, 1]])
3655|
3656|        See Also
3657|        ========
3658|
3659|        cholesky
3660|        LDLdecomposition
3661|        LUdecomposition
3662|        QRsolve
3663|        """
3664|        cls = self.__class__
3665|        mat = self.as_mutable()
3666|
3667|        if not mat.rows >= mat.cols:
3668|            raise MatrixError(
3669|                "The number of rows must be greater than columns")
3670|        n = mat.rows
3671|        m = mat.cols
3672|        rank = n
3673|        row_reduced = mat.rref()[0]
3674|        for i in range(row_reduced.rows):
3675|            if row_reduced.row(i).norm() == 0:
3676|                rank -= 1
3677|        if not rank == mat.cols:
3678|            raise MatrixError("The rank of the matrix must match the columns")
3679|        Q, R = mat.zeros(n, m), mat.zeros(m)
3680|        for j in range(m):  # for each column vector
3681|            tmp = mat[:, j]  # take original v
3682|            for i in range(j):
3683|                # subtract the project of mat on new vector
3684|                tmp -= Q[:, i] * mat[:, j].dot(Q[:, i])
3685|                tmp.expand()
3686|            # normalize it
3687|            R[j, j] = tmp.norm()
3688|            Q[:, j] = tmp / R[j, j]
3689|            if Q[:, j].norm() != 1:
3690|                raise NotImplementedError(
3691|                    "Could not normalize the vector %d." % j)
3692|            for i in range(j):
3693|                R[i, j] = Q[:, i].dot(mat[:, j])
3694|        return cls(Q), cls(R)

3696|    def QRsolve(self, b):
3697|        """Solve the linear system 'Ax = b'.
3698|
3699|        'self' is the matrix 'A', the method argument is the vector
3700|        'b'.  The method returns the solution vector 'x'.  If 'b' is a
3701|        matrix, the system is solved for each column of 'b' and the
3702|        return value is a matrix of the same shape as 'b'.
3703|
3704|        This method is slower (approximately by a factor of 2) but
3705|        more stable for floating-point arithmetic than the LUsolve method.
3706|        However, LUsolve usually uses an exact arithmetic, so you don't need
3707|        to use QRsolve.
3708|
3709|        This is mainly for educational purposes and symbolic matrices, for real
3710|        (or complex) matrices use mpmath.qr_solve.
3711|
3712|        See Also
3713|        ========
3714|
3715|        lower_triangular_solve
3716|        upper_triangular_solve
3717|        gauss_jordan_solve
3718|        cholesky_solve
3719|        diagonal_solve
3720|        LDLsolve
3721|        LUsolve
3722|        pinv_solve
3723|        QRdecomposition
3724|        """
3725|
3726|        Q, R = self.as_mutable().QRdecomposition()
3727|        y = Q.T * b
3728|
3729|        # back substitution to solve R*x = y:
3730|        # We build up the result "backwards" in the vector 'x' and reverse it
3731|        # only in the end.
3732|        x = []
3733|        n = R.rows
3734|        for j in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
3735|            tmp = y[j, :]
3736|            for k in range(j + 1, n):
3737|                tmp -= R[j, k] * x[n - 1 - k]
3738|            x.append(tmp / R[j, j])
3739|        return self._new([row._mat for row in reversed(x)])
3740|
3741|    def solve_least_squares(self, rhs, method='CH'):
3742|        """Return the least-square fit to the data.
3743|
3744|        By default the cholesky_solve routine is used (method='CH'); other
3745|        methods of matrix inversion can be used. To find out which are
3746|        available, see the docstring of the .inv() method.
3747|
3748|        Examples
3749|        ========
3750|
3751|        >>> from sympy.matrices import Matrix, ones
3752|        >>> A = Matrix([1, 2, 3])
3753|        >>> B = Matrix([2, 3, 4])
3754|        >>> S = Matrix(A.row_join(B))
3755|        >>> S
3756|        Matrix([
3757|        [1, 2],
3758|        [2, 3],
