216|def posify(eq):
217|    """Return ``eq`` (with generic symbols made positive) and a
218|    dictionary containing the mapping between the old and new
219|    symbols.
220|
221|    Explanation
222|    ===========
223|
224|    Any symbol that has positive=None will be replaced with a positive dummy
225|    symbol having the same name. This replacement will allow more symbolic
226|    processing of expressions, especially those involving powers and
227|    logarithms.
228|
229|    A dictionary that can be sent to subs to restore ``eq`` to its original
230|    symbols is also returned.
231|
232|    >>> from sympy import posify, Symbol, log, solve
233|    >>> from sympy.abc import x
234|    >>> posify(x + Symbol('p', positive=True) + Symbol('n', negative=True))
235|    (_x + n + p, {_x: x})
236|
237|    >>> eq = 1/x
238|    >>> log(eq).expand()
239|    log(1/x)
240|    >>> log(posify(eq)[0]).expand()
241|    -log(_x)
242|    >>> p, rep = posify(eq)
243|    >>> log(p).expand().subs(rep)
244|    -log(x)
245|
246|    It is possible to apply the same transformations to an iterable
247|    of expressions:
248|
249|    >>> eq = x**2 - 4
250|    >>> solve(eq, x)
251|    [-2, 2]
252|    >>> eq_x, reps = posify([eq, x]); eq_x
253|    [_x**2 - 4, _x]
254|    >>> solve(*eq_x)
255|    [2]
256|    """
257|    eq = sympify(eq)
258|    if iterable(eq):
259|        f = type(eq)
260|        eq = list(eq)
261|        syms = set()
262|        for e in eq:
263|            syms = syms.union(e.atoms(Symbol))
264|        reps = {}
265|        for s in syms:
266|            reps.update({v: k for k, v in posify(s)[1].items()})
267|        for i, e in enumerate(eq):
268|            eq[i] = e.subs(reps)
269|        return f(eq), {r: s for s, r in reps.items()}
270|
271|    reps = {s: Dummy(s.name, positive=True, **s.assumptions0)
272|                 for s in eq.free_symbols if s.is_positive is None}
273|    eq = eq.subs(reps)
274|    return eq, {r: s for s, r in reps.items()}

411|def simplify(expr, ratio=1.7, measure=count_ops, rational=False, inverse=False, doit=True, **kwargs):
412|    """Simplifies the given expression.
413|
414|    Explanation
415|    ===========
416|
417|    Simplification is not a well defined term and the exact strategies
418|    this function tries can change in the future versions of SymPy. If
419|    your algorithm relies on "simplification" (whatever it is), try to
420|    determine what you need exactly  -  is it powsimp()?, radsimp()?,
421|    together()?, logcombine()?, or something else? And use this particular
422|    function directly, because those are well defined and thus your algorithm
423|    will be robust.
424|
425|    Nonetheless, especially for interactive use, or when you don't know
426|    anything about the structure of the expression, simplify() tries to apply
427|    intelligent heuristics to make the input expression "simpler".  For
428|    example:
429|
430|    >>> from sympy import simplify, cos, sin
431|    >>> from sympy.abc import x, y
432|    >>> a = (x + x**2)/(x*sin(y)**2 + x*cos(y)**2)
433|    >>> a
434|    (x**2 + x)/(x*sin(y)**2 + x*cos(y)**2)
435|    >>> simplify(a)
436|    x + 1
437|
438|    Note that we could have obtained the same result by using specific
439|    simplification functions:
440|
441|    >>> from sympy import trigsimp, cancel
442|    >>> trigsimp(a)
443|    (x**2 + x)/x
444|    >>> cancel(_)
445|    x + 1
446|
447|    In some cases, applying :func:`simplify` may actually result in some more
448|    complicated expression. The default ``ratio=1.7`` prevents more extreme
449|    cases: if (result length)/(input length) > ratio, then input is returned
450|    unmodified.  The ``measure`` parameter lets you specify the function used
451|    to determine how complex an expression is.  The function should take a
452|    single argument as an expression and return a number such that if
453|    expression ``a`` is more complex than expression ``b``, then
454|    ``measure(a) > measure(b)``.  The default measure function is
455|    :func:`~.count_ops`, which returns the total number of operations in the
456|    expression.
457|
458|    For example, if ``ratio=1``, ``simplify`` output can't be longer
459|    than input.
460|
461|    ::
462|
463|        >>> from sympy import sqrt, simplify, count_ops, oo
464|        >>> root = 1/(sqrt(2)+3)
465|
466|    Since ``simplify(root)`` would result in a slightly longer expression,
467|    root is returned unchanged instead::
468|
469|       >>> simplify(root, ratio=1) == root
470|       True
471|
472|    If ``ratio=oo``, simplify will be applied anyway::
473|
474|        >>> count_ops(simplify(root, ratio=oo)) > count_ops(root)
475|        True
476|
477|    Note that the shortest expression is not necessary the simplest, so
478|    setting ``ratio`` to 1 may not be a good idea.
479|    Heuristically, the default value ``ratio=1.7`` seems like a reasonable
480|    choice.
481|
482|    You can easily define your own measure function based on what you feel
483|    should represent the "size" or "complexity" of the input expression.  Note
484|    that some choices, such as ``lambda expr: len(str(expr))`` may appear to be
485|    good metrics, but have other problems (in this case, the measure function
486|    may slow down simplify too much for very large expressions).  If you don't
487|    know what a good metric would be, the default, ``count_ops``, is a good
488|    one.
489|
490|    For example:
491|
492|    >>> from sympy import symbols, log
493|    >>> a, b = symbols('a b', positive=True)
494|    >>> g = log(a) + log(b) + log(a)*log(1/b)
495|    >>> h = simplify(g)
496|    >>> h
497|    log(a*b**(1 - log(a)))
498|    >>> count_ops(g)
499|    8
500|    >>> count_ops(h)
501|    5
502|
503|    So you can see that ``h`` is simpler than ``g`` using the count_ops metric.
504|    However, we may not like how ``simplify`` (in this case, using
505|    ``logcombine``) has created the ``b**(log(1/a) + 1)`` term.  A simple way
506|    to reduce this would be to give more weight to powers as operations in
507|    ``count_ops``.  We can do this by using the ``visual=True`` option:
508|
509|    >>> print(count_ops(g, visual=True))
510|    2*ADD + DIV + 4*LOG + MUL
511|    >>> print(count_ops(h, visual=True))
512|    2*LOG + MUL + POW + SUB
513|
514|    >>> from sympy import Symbol, S
515|    >>> def my_measure(expr):
516|    ...     POW = Symbol('POW')
517|    ...     # Discourage powers by giving POW a weight of 10
518|    ...     count = count_ops(expr, visual=True).subs(POW, 10)
519|    ...     # Every other operation gets a weight of 1 (the default)
520|    ...     count = count.replace(Symbol, type(S.One))
521|    ...     return count
522|    >>> my_measure(g)
523|    8
524|    >>> my_measure(h)
525|    14
526|    >>> 15./8 > 1.7 # 1.7 is the default ratio
527|    True
528|    >>> simplify(g, measure=my_measure)
529|    -log(a)*log(b) + log(a) + log(b)
530|

534|    from the input expression by doing this.

I am seeing weird behavior with `subs` for particular expressions with hyperbolic sinusoids with piecewise arguments. When applying `subs`, I obtain an unexpected `PolynomialError`. You can pretend the expression below has a `+ 1` at the end, but below is the MWE that I could produce.

See the expression below, and the conditions in which the exception arises.

Sympy version: 1.8.dev

```python
from sympy import *
from sympy.core.cache import clear_cache

x, y, z = symbols('x y z')

clear_cache()
expr = exp(sinh(Piecewise((x, y > x), (y, True)) / z))
# This works fine
expr.subs({1: 1.0})

x, y, z = symbols('x y z', real=True)
expr = exp(sinh(Piecewise((x, y > x), (y, True)) / z))
# This fails with "PolynomialError: Piecewise generators do not make sense"
expr.subs({1: 1.0})  # error

expr.subs({1: 1.0})

- The error only (AFAIK) happens with `cosh` or `tanh` in place of `sinh`, otherwise it succeeds
- The error goes away if removing the division by `z`
- The error goes away if removing `exp` (but stays for most unary functions, `sin`, `log`, etc.)
- The error only happens with real symbols for `x` and `y` (`z` does not have to be real)

Not too sure how to debug this one.

570|    def _print_Sum(self, expr):
571|        ascii_mode = not self._use_unicode
572|
573|        def asum(hrequired, lower, upper, use_ascii):
574|            def adjust(s, wid=None, how='<^>'):
575|                if not wid or len(s) > wid:
576|                    return s
577|                need = wid - len(s)
578|                if how in ('<^>', "<") or how not in list('<^>'):
579|                    return s + ' '*need
580|                half = need//2
581|                lead = ' '*half
582|                if how == ">":
583|                    return " "*need + s
584|                return lead + s + ' '*(need - len(lead))
585|
586|            h = max(hrequired, 2)
587|            d = h//2
588|            w = d + 1
589|            more = hrequired % 2
590|
591|            lines = []
592|            if use_ascii:
593|                lines.append("_"*(w) + ' ')
594|                lines.append(r"\%s`" % (' '*(w - 1)))
595|                for i in range(1, d):
596|                    lines.append('%s\\%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
597|                if more:
598|                    lines.append('%s)%s' % (' '*(d), ' '*(w - d)))
599|                for i in reversed(range(1, d)):
600|                    lines.append('%s/%s' % (' '*i, ' '*(w - i)))
601|                lines.append("/" + "_"*(w - 1) + ',')
602|                return d, h + more, lines, more
603|            else:
604|                w = w + more
605|                d = d + more
606|                vsum = vobj('sum', 4)
607|                lines.append("_"*(w))
608|                for i in range(0, d):
609|                    lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[2], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
610|                for i in reversed(range(0, d)):
611|                    lines.append('%s%s%s' % (' '*i, vsum[4], ' '*(w - i - 1)))
612|                lines.append(vsum[8]*(w))
613|                return d, h + 2*more, lines, more
614|
615|        f = expr.function
616|
617|        prettyF = self._print(f)
618|
619|        if f.is_Add:  # add parens
620|            prettyF = prettyForm(*prettyF.parens())
621|
622|        H = prettyF.height() + 2
623|
624|        # \sum \sum \sum ...
625|        first = True
626|        max_upper = 0
627|        sign_height = 0
628|
629|        for lim in expr.limits:
630|            prettyLower, prettyUpper = self.__print_SumProduct_Limits(lim)
631|
632|            max_upper = max(max_upper, prettyUpper.height())
633|
634|            # Create sum sign based on the height of the argument
635|            d, h, slines, adjustment = asum(
636|                H, prettyLower.width(), prettyUpper.width(), ascii_mode)
637|            prettySign = stringPict('')
638|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.stack(*slines))
639|
640|            if first:
641|                sign_height = prettySign.height()
642|
643|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.above(prettyUpper))
644|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.below(prettyLower))
645|
646|            if first:
647|                # change F baseline so it centers on the sign
648|                prettyF.baseline -= d - (prettyF.height()//2 -
649|                                         prettyF.baseline)
650|                first = False
651|
652|            # put padding to the right
653|            pad = stringPict('')
654|            pad = prettyForm(*pad.stack(*[' ']*h))
655|            prettySign = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(pad))
656|            # put the present prettyF to the right
657|            prettyF = prettyForm(*prettySign.right(prettyF))
658|
659|        # adjust baseline of ascii mode sigma with an odd height so that it is
660|        # exactly through the center
661|        ascii_adjustment = ascii_mode if not adjustment else 0
662|        prettyF.baseline = max_upper + sign_height//2 + ascii_adjustment
663|

1976|                     (isinstance(x, Pow) and isinstance(x.base, Quantity)))
1977|
1978|        # Gather terms for numerator/denominator

1995|        b = [self._print(bi) for bi in b]
1996|

2006|    def _print_nth_root(self, base, root):
2007|        bpretty = self._print(base)
2008|
2009|        # In very simple cases, use a single-char root sign
2010|        if (self._settings['use_unicode_sqrt_char'] and self._use_unicode
2011|            and root == 2 and bpretty.height() == 1
2012|            and (bpretty.width() == 1
2013|                 or (base.is_Integer and base.is_nonnegative))):
2014|            return prettyForm(*bpretty.left('\N{SQUARE ROOT}'))
2015|
2016|        # Construct root sign, start with the \/ shape
2017|        _zZ = xobj('/', 1)
2018|        rootsign = xobj('\\', 1) + _zZ
2019|        # Constructing the number to put on root
2020|        rpretty = self._print(root)
2021|        # roots look bad if they are not a single line
2022|        if rpretty.height() != 1:
2023|            return self._print(base)**self._print(1/root)
2024|        # If power is half, no number should appear on top of root sign
2025|        exp = '' if root == 2 else str(rpretty).ljust(2)
2026|        if len(exp) > 2:
2027|            rootsign = ' '*(len(exp) - 2) + rootsign
2028|        # Stack the exponent
2029|        rootsign = stringPict(exp + '\n' + rootsign)
2030|        rootsign.baseline = 0
2031|        # Diagonal: length is one less than height of base
2032|        linelength = bpretty.height() - 1
2033|        diagonal = stringPict('\n'.join(

2041|        # Det the baseline to match contents to fix the height

2043|        rootsign.baseline = max(1, bpretty.baseline)
2044|        #build result

1125|    assumed to have continuous derivatives up to the order asked.
1126|
1127|    Derivative wrt non-Symbols:
1128|
1129|    For the most part, one may not differentiate wrt non-symbols.
1130|    For example, we do not allow differentiation wrt `x*y` because
1131|    there are multiple ways of structurally defining where x*y appears
1132|    in an expression: a very strict definition would make
1133|    (x*y*z).diff(x*y) == 0. Derivatives wrt defined functions (like
1134|    cos(x)) are not allowed, either:
1135|
1136|        >>> (x*y*z).diff(x*y)
1137|        Traceback (most recent call last):
1138|        ...
1139|        ValueError: Can't calculate derivative wrt x*y.
1140|
1141|    To make it easier to work with variational calculus, however,
1142|    derivatives wrt AppliedUndef and Derivatives are allowed.
1143|    For example, in the Euler-Lagrange method one may write
1144|    F(t, u, v) where u = f(t) and v = f'(t). These variables can be
1145|    written explicitly as functions of time::
1146|
1147|        >>> from sympy.abc import t
1148|        >>> F = Function('F')
1149|        >>> U = f(t)
1150|        >>> V = U.diff(t)
1151|
1152|    The derivative wrt f(t) can be obtained directly:
1153|
1154|        >>> direct = F(t, U, V).diff(U)
1155|
1156|    When differentiation wrt a non-Symbol is attempted, the non-Symbol
1157|    is temporarily converted to a Symbol while the differentiation
1158|    is performed and the same answer is obtained:
1159|
1160|        >>> indirect = F(t, U, V).subs(U, x).diff(x).subs(x, U)
1161|        >>> assert direct == indirect
1162|
1163|    The implication of this non-symbol replacement is that all
1164|    functions are treated as independent of other functions and the
1165|    symbols are independent of the functions that contain them::
1166|
1167|        >>> x.diff(f(x))
1168|        0
1169|        >>> g(x).diff(f(x))
1170|        0
1171|
1172|    It also means that derivatives are assumed to depend only
1173|    on the variables of differentiation, not on anything contained
1174|    within the expression being differentiated::
1175|
1176|        >>> F = f(x)
1177|        >>> Fx = F.diff(x)
1178|        >>> Fx.diff(F)  # derivative depends on x, not F
1179|        0
1180|        >>> Fxx = Fx.diff(x)
1181|        >>> Fxx.diff(Fx)  # derivative depends on x, not Fx
1182|        0
1183|
1184|    The last example can be made explicit by showing the replacement
1185|    of Fx in Fxx with y:
1186|
1187|        >>> Fxx.subs(Fx, y)
1188|        Derivative(y, x)
1189|
1190|        Since that in itself will evaluate to zero, differentiating
1191|        wrt Fx will also be zero:
1192|
1193|        >>> _.doit()
1194|        0
1195|
1196|    Replacing undefined functions with concrete expressions
1197|
1198|    One must be careful to replace undefined functions with expressions
1199|    that contain variables consistent with the function definition and
1200|    the variables of differentiation or else insconsistent result will
1201|    be obtained. Consider the following example:
1202|
1203|    >>> eq = f(x)*g(y)
1204|    >>> eq.subs(f(x), x*y).diff(x, y).doit()
1205|    y*Derivative(g(y), y) + g(y)
1206|    >>> eq.diff(x, y).subs(f(x), x*y).doit()
1207|    y*Derivative(g(y), y)
1208|
1209|    The results differ because `f(x)` was replaced with an expression
1210|    that involved both variables of differentiation. In the abstract
1211|    case, differentiation of `f(x)` by `y` is 0; in the concrete case,
1212|    the presence of `y` made that derivative nonvanishing and produced
1213|    the extra `g(y)` term.
1214|
1215|    Defining differentiation for an object
1216|
1217|    An object must define ._eval_derivative(symbol) method that returns
1218|    the differentiation result. This function only needs to consider the
1219|    non-trivial case where expr contains symbol and it should call the diff()
1220|    method internally (not _eval_derivative); Derivative should be the only
1221|    one to call _eval_derivative.
1222|
1223|    Any class can allow derivatives to be taken with respect to
1224|    itself (while indicating its scalar nature). See the
1225|    docstring of Expr._diff_wrt.
1226|
1227|    See Also
1228|    ========
1229|    _sort_variable_count
1230|    """
1231|
1232|    is_Derivative = True

1234|    @property
1235|    def _diff_wrt(self):
1236|        """An expression may be differentiated wrt a Derivative if
1237|        it is in elementary form.
1238|
1239|        Examples
1240|        ========
1241|
1242|        >>> from sympy import Function, Derivative, cos
1243|        >>> from sympy.abc import x
1244|        >>> f = Function('f')
1245|
1246|        >>> Derivative(f(x), x)._diff_wrt
1247|        True
1248|        >>> Derivative(cos(x), x)._diff_wrt
1249|        False
1250|        >>> Derivative(x + 1, x)._diff_wrt
1251|        False
1252|
1253|        A Derivative might be an unevaluated form of what will not be
1254|        a valid variable of differentiation if evaluated. For example,
1255|
1256|        >>> Derivative(f(f(x)), x).doit()
1257|        Derivative(f(x), x)*Derivative(f(f(x)), f(x))
1258|
1259|        Such an expression will present the same ambiguities as arise
1260|        when dealing with any other product, like ``2*x``, so ``_diff_wrt``
1261|        is False:
1262|
1263|        >>> Derivative(f(f(x)), x)._diff_wrt
1264|        False
1265|        """
1266|        return self.expr._diff_wrt and isinstance(self.doit(), Derivative)

1268|    def __new__(cls, expr, *variables, **kwargs):
1269|
1270|        from sympy.matrices.common import MatrixCommon
1271|        from sympy import Integer, MatrixExpr
1272|        from sympy.tensor.array import Array, NDimArray
1273|        from sympy.utilities.misc import filldedent
1274|
1275|        expr = sympify(expr)
1276|        symbols_or_none = getattr(expr, "free_symbols", None)
1277|        has_symbol_set = isinstance(symbols_or_none, set)
1278|
1279|        if not has_symbol_set:
1280|            raise ValueError(filldedent('''
1281|                Since there are no variables in the expression %s,
1282|                it cannot be differentiated.''' % expr))
1283|
1284|        # determine value for variables if it wasn't given
1285|        if not variables:
1286|            variables = expr.free_symbols
1287|            if len(variables) != 1:
1288|                if expr.is_number:
1289|                    return S.Zero
1290|                if len(variables) == 0:
1291|                    raise ValueError(filldedent('''
1292|                        Since there are no variables in the expression,
1293|                        the variable(s) of differentiation must be supplied
1294|                        to differentiate %s''' % expr))
1295|                else:
1296|                    raise ValueError(filldedent('''
1297|                        Since there is more than one variable in the
1298|                        expression, the variable(s) of differentiation
1299|                        must be supplied to differentiate %s''' % expr))
1300|
1301|        # Standardize the variables by sympifying them:
1302|        variables = list(sympify(variables))
1303|
1304|        # Split the list of variables into a list of the variables we are diff
1305|        # wrt, where each element of the list has the form (s, count) where
1306|        # s is the entity to diff wrt and count is the order of the
1307|        # derivative.
1308|        variable_count = []
1309|        array_likes = (tuple, list, Tuple)
1310|
1311|        for i, v in enumerate(variables):
1312|            if isinstance(v, Integer):
1313|                if i == 0:
1314|                    raise ValueError("First variable cannot be a number: %i" % v)
1315|                count = v
1316|                prev, prevcount = variable_count[-1]
1317|                if prevcount != 1:
1318|                    raise TypeError("tuple {} followed by number {}".format((prev, prevcount), v))
1319|                if count == 0:
1320|                    variable_count.pop()
1321|                else:
1322|                    variable_count[-1] = Tuple(prev, count)
1323|            else:
1324|                if isinstance(v, array_likes):
1325|                    if len(v) == 0:
1326|                        # Ignore empty tuples: Derivative(expr, ... , (), ... )
1327|                        continue
1328|                    if isinstance(v[0], array_likes):
1329|                        # Derive by array: Derivative(expr, ... , [[x, y, z]], ... )
1330|                        if len(v) == 1:
1331|                            v = Array(v[0])
1332|                            count = 1
1333|                        else:
1334|                            v, count = v
1335|                            v = Array(v)
1336|                    else:
1337|                        v, count = v
1338|                    if count == 0:
1339|                        continue
1340|                elif isinstance(v, UndefinedFunction):
1341|                    raise TypeError(
1342|                        "cannot differentiate wrt "
1343|                        "UndefinedFunction: %s" % v)
1344|                else:
1345|                    count = 1
1346|                variable_count.append(Tuple(v, count))
1347|
1348|        # light evaluation of contiguous, identical
1349|        # items: (x, 1), (x, 1) -> (x, 2)
1350|        merged = []
1351|        for t in variable_count:
1352|            v, c = t
1353|            if c.is_negative:
1354|                raise ValueError(
1355|                    'order of differentiation must be nonnegative')
1356|            if merged and merged[-1][0] == v:
1357|                c += merged[-1][1]
1358|                if not c:
1359|                    merged.pop()
1360|                else:
1361|                    merged[-1] = Tuple(v, c)
1362|            else:
1363|                merged.append(t)
1364|        variable_count = merged
1365|
1366|        # sanity check of variables of differentation; we waited
1367|        # until the counts were computed since some variables may
1368|        # have been removed because the count was 0
1369|        for v, c in variable_count:
1370|            # v must have _diff_wrt True
1371|            if not v._diff_wrt:
1372|                __ = ''  # filler to make error message neater
1373|                raise ValueError(filldedent('''
1374|                    Can't calculate derivative wrt %s.%s''' % (v,
1375|                    __)))
1376|
1377|        # We make a special case for 0th derivative, because there is no
1378|        # good way to unambiguously print this.
1379|        if len(variable_count) == 0:
1380|            return expr
1381|
1382|        evaluate = kwargs.get('evaluate', False)
1383|
1384|        if evaluate:
1385|            if isinstance(expr, Derivative):
1386|                expr = expr.canonical
1387|            variable_count = [
1388|                (v.canonical if isinstance(v, Derivative) else v, c)
1389|                for v, c in variable_count]
1390|
1391|            # Look for a quick exit if there are symbols that don't appear in
1392|            # expression at all. Note, this cannot check non-symbols like
1393|            # Derivatives as those can be created by intermediate
1394|            # derivatives.
1395|            zero = False
1396|            free = expr.free_symbols
1397|            for v, c in variable_count:
1398|                vfree = v.free_symbols
1399|                if c.is_positive and vfree:
1400|                    if isinstance(v, AppliedUndef):
1401|                        # these match exactly since
1402|                        # x.diff(f(x)) == g(x).diff(f(x)) == 0
1403|                        # and are not created by differentiation
1404|                        D = Dummy()
1405|                        if not expr.xreplace({v: D}).has(D):
1406|                            zero = True
1407|                            break
1408|                    elif isinstance(v, MatrixExpr):
1409|                        zero = False
1410|                        break
1411|                    elif isinstance(v, Symbol) and v not in free:
1412|                        zero = True
1413|                        break
1414|                    else:
1415|                        if not free & vfree:
1416|                            # e.g. v is IndexedBase or Matrix
1417|                            zero = True
1418|                            break
1419|            if zero:
1420|                return cls._get_zero_with_shape_like(expr)
1421|
1422|            # make the order of symbols canonical
1423|            #TODO: check if assumption of discontinuous derivatives exist
1424|            variable_count = cls._sort_variable_count(variable_count)
1425|
1426|        # denest
1427|        if isinstance(expr, Derivative):
1428|            variable_count = list(expr.variable_count) + variable_count
1429|            expr = expr.expr
1430|            return _derivative_dispatch(expr, *variable_count, **kwargs)
1431|
1432|        # we return here if evaluate is False or if there is no
1433|        # _eval_derivative method
1434|        if not evaluate or not hasattr(expr, '_eval_derivative'):
1435|            # return an unevaluated Derivative
1436|            if evaluate and variable_count == [(expr, 1)] and expr.is_scalar:
1437|                # special hack providing evaluation for classes
1438|                # that have defined is_scalar=True but have no
1439|                # _eval_derivative defined
1440|                return S.One
1441|            return Expr.__new__(cls, expr, *variable_count)
1442|
1443|        # evaluate the derivative by calling _eval_derivative method
1444|        # of expr for each variable
1445|        # -------------------------------------------------------------
1446|        nderivs = 0  # how many derivatives were performed
1447|        unhandled = []
1448|        for i, (v, count) in enumerate(variable_count):
1449|
1450|            old_expr = expr
1451|            old_v = None
1452|
1453|            is_symbol = v.is_symbol or isinstance(v,
1454|                (Iterable, Tuple, MatrixCommon, NDimArray))
1455|
1456|            if not is_symbol:
1457|                old_v = v
1458|                v = Dummy('xi')
1459|                expr = expr.xreplace({old_v: v})
1460|                # Derivatives and UndefinedFunctions are independent
1461|                # of all others
1462|                clashing = not (isinstance(old_v, Derivative) or \
1463|                    isinstance(old_v, AppliedUndef))
1464|                if not v in expr.free_symbols and not clashing:
1465|                    return expr.diff(v)  # expr's version of 0
1466|                if not old_v.is_scalar and not hasattr(
1467|                        old_v, '_eval_derivative'):
1468|                    # special hack providing evaluation for classes
1469|                    # that have defined is_scalar=True but have no
1470|                    # _eval_derivative defined
1471|                    expr *= old_v.diff(old_v)
1472|
1473|            obj = cls._dispatch_eval_derivative_n_times(expr, v, count)
1474|            if obj is not None and obj.is_zero:
1475|                return obj
1476|
1477|            nderivs += count
1478|
1479|            if old_v is not None:
1480|                if obj is not None:
1481|                    # remove the dummy that was used
1482|                    obj = obj.subs(v, old_v)
1483|                # restore expr
1484|                expr = old_expr
1485|
1486|            if obj is None:
1487|                # we've already checked for quick-exit conditions
1488|                # that give 0 so the remaining variables
1489|                # are contained in the expression but the expression
1490|                # did not compute a derivative so we stop taking
1491|                # derivatives
1492|                unhandled = variable_count[i:]
1493|                break
1494|
1495|            expr = obj
1496|
1497|        # what we have so far can be made canonical
1498|        expr = expr.replace(
1499|            lambda x: isinstance(x, Derivative),
1500|            lambda x: x.canonical)
1501|
1502|        if unhandled:
1503|            if isinstance(expr, Derivative):
1504|                unhandled = list(expr.variable_count) + unhandled

1507|
1508|        if (nderivs > 1) == True and kwargs.get('simplify', True):

1510|            from sympy.simplify.simplify import signsimp
1511|            expr = factor_terms(signsimp(expr))

1519|    @classmethod
1520|    def _sort_variable_count(cls, vc):
1521|        """
1522|        Sort (variable, count) pairs into canonical order while
1523|        retaining order of variables that do not commute during
1524|        differentiation:
1525|
1526|        * symbols and functions commute with each other
1527|        * derivatives commute with each other
1528|        * a derivative doesn't commute with anything it contains
1529|        * any other object is not allowed to commute if it has
1530|          free symbols in common with another object
1531|
1532|        Examples
1533|        ========
1534|
1535|        >>> from sympy import Derivative, Function, symbols
1536|        >>> vsort = Derivative._sort_variable_count
1537|        >>> x, y, z = symbols('x y z')
1538|        >>> f, g, h = symbols('f g h', cls=Function)
1539|
1540|        Contiguous items are collapsed into one pair:
1541|
1542|        >>> vsort([(x, 1), (x, 1)])
1543|        [(x, 2)]
1544|        >>> vsort([(y, 1), (f(x), 1), (y, 1), (f(x), 1)])
1545|        [(y, 2), (f(x), 2)]
1546|
1547|        Ordering is canonical.
1548|
1549|        >>> def vsort0(*v):
1550|        ...     # docstring helper to
1551|        ...     # change vi -> (vi, 0), sort, and return vi vals
1552|        ...     return [i[0] for i in vsort([(i, 0) for i in v])]
1553|
1554|        >>> vsort0(y, x)
1555|        [x, y]
1556|        >>> vsort0(g(y), g(x), f(y))
1557|        [f(y), g(x), g(y)]
1558|
1559|        Symbols are sorted as far to the left as possible but never
1560|        move to the left of a derivative having the same symbol in
1561|        its variables; the same applies to AppliedUndef which are
1562|        always sorted after Symbols:
1563|
1564|        >>> dfx = f(x).diff(x)
1565|        >>> assert vsort0(dfx, y) == [y, dfx]
1566|        >>> assert vsort0(dfx, x) == [dfx, x]
1567|        """
1568|        from sympy.utilities.iterables import uniq, topological_sort
1569|        if not vc:
1570|            return []
1571|        vc = list(vc)
1572|        if len(vc) == 1:
1573|            return [Tuple(*vc[0])]
1574|        V = list(range(len(vc)))
1575|        E = []
1576|        v = lambda i: vc[i][0]
1577|        D = Dummy()
1578|        def _block(d, v, wrt=False):
1579|            # return True if v should not come before d else False
1580|            if d == v:
1581|                return wrt
1582|            if d.is_Symbol:
1583|                return False
1584|            if isinstance(d, Derivative):
1585|                # a derivative blocks if any of it's variables contain
1586|                # v; the wrt flag will return True for an exact match
1587|                # and will cause an AppliedUndef to block if v is in
1588|                # the arguments
1589|                if any(_block(k, v, wrt=True)
1590|                        for k in d._wrt_variables):
1591|                    return True
1592|                return False
1593|            if not wrt and isinstance(d, AppliedUndef):
1594|                return False
1595|            if v.is_Symbol:
1596|                return v in d.free_symbols
1597|            if isinstance(v, AppliedUndef):
1598|                return _block(d.xreplace({v: D}), D)
1599|            return d.free_symbols & v.free_symbols
1600|        for i in range(len(vc)):
1601|            for j in range(i):
1602|                if _block(v(j), v(i)):
1603|                    E.append((j,i))
1604|        # this is the default ordering to use in case of ties
1605|        O = dict(zip(ordered(uniq([i for i, c in vc])), range(len(vc))))
1606|        ix = topological_sort((V, E), key=lambda i: O[v(i)])
1607|        # merge counts of contiguously identical items
1608|        merged = []
1609|        for v, c in [vc[i] for i in ix]:
1610|            if merged and merged[-1][0] == v:
1611|                merged[-1][1] += c
1612|            else:
1613|                merged.append([v, c])
1614|        return [Tuple(*i) for i in merged]

1617|        return self.expr.is_commutative

1619|    def _eval_derivative(self, v):
1620|        # If v (the variable of differentiation) is not in
1621|        # self.variables, we might be able to take the derivative.
1622|        if v not in self._wrt_variables:
1623|            dedv = self.expr.diff(v)
1624|            if isinstance(dedv, Derivative):
1625|                return dedv.func(dedv.expr, *(self.variable_count + dedv.variable_count))
1626|            # dedv (d(self.expr)/dv) could have simplified things such that the
1627|            # derivative wrt things in self.variables can now be done. Thus,
1628|            # we set evaluate=True to see if there are any other derivatives
1629|            # that can be done. The most common case is when dedv is a simple
1630|            # number so that the derivative wrt anything else will vanish.
1631|            return self.func(dedv, *self.variables, evaluate=True)
1632|        # In this case v was in self.variables so the derivative wrt v has
1633|        # already been attempted and was not computed, either because it
1634|        # couldn't be or evaluate=False originally.
1635|        variable_count = list(self.variable_count)
1636|        variable_count.append((v, 1))
1637|        return self.func(self.expr, *variable_count, evaluate=False)

1639|    def doit(self, **hints):
1640|        expr = self.expr
1641|        if hints.get('deep', True):
1642|            expr = expr.doit(**hints)
1643|        hints['evaluate'] = True
1644|        rv = self.func(expr, *self.variable_count, **hints)
1645|        if rv!= self and rv.has(Derivative):
1646|            rv =  rv.doit(**hints)
1647|        return rv

1649|    @_sympifyit('z0', NotImplementedError)
1650|    def doit_numerically(self, z0):
1651|        """
1652|        Evaluate the derivative at z numerically.
1653|
1654|        When we can represent derivatives at a point, this should be folded
1655|        into the normal evalf. For now, we need a special method.
1656|        """
1657|        if len(self.free_symbols) != 1 or len(self.variables) != 1:
1658|            raise NotImplementedError('partials and higher order derivatives')
1659|        z = list(self.free_symbols)[0]
1660|
1661|        def eval(x):
1662|            f0 = self.expr.subs(z, Expr._from_mpmath(x, prec=mpmath.mp.prec))
1663|            f0 = f0.evalf(mlib.libmpf.prec_to_dps(mpmath.mp.prec))
1664|            return f0._to_mpmath(mpmath.mp.prec)
1665|        return Expr._from_mpmath(mpmath.diff(eval,
1666|                                             z0._to_mpmath(mpmath.mp.prec)),
1667|                                 mpmath.mp.prec)

1703|    def free_symbols(self):

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Python code printer not respecting tuple with one element
Hi,

Thanks for the recent updates in SymPy! I'm trying to update my code to use SymPy 1.10 but ran into an issue with the Python code printer. MWE:


```python
import inspect
from sympy import lambdify

inspect.getsource(lambdify([], tuple([1])))
```
SymPy 1.9 and under outputs:
```
'def _lambdifygenerated():\n    return (1,)\n'
```

But SymPy 1.10 gives

```
'def _lambdifygenerated():\n    return (1)\n'
```
Note the missing comma after `1` that causes an integer to be returned instead of a tuple. 

For tuples with two or more elements, the generated code is correct:
```python
inspect.getsource(lambdify([], tuple([1, 2])))
```
In SymPy  1.10 and under, outputs:

```
'def _lambdifygenerated():\n    return (1, 2)\n'
```
This result is expected.

Not sure if this is a regression. As this breaks my program which assumes the return type to always be a tuple, could you suggest a workaround from the code generation side? Thank you.

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Bug in expand of TensorProduct + Workaround + Fix
### Error description
The expansion of a TensorProduct object stops incomplete if summands in the tensor product factors have (scalar) factors, e.g.
```
from sympy import *
from sympy.physics.quantum import *
U = Operator('U')
V = Operator('V')
P = TensorProduct(2*U - V, U + V)
print(P) 
# (2*U - V)x(U + V)
print(P.expand(tensorproduct=True)) 
#result: 2*Ux(U + V) - Vx(U + V) #expansion has missed 2nd tensor factor and is incomplete
```
This is clearly not the expected behaviour. It also effects other functions that rely on .expand(tensorproduct=True), as e.g. qapply() .

### Work around
Repeat .expand(tensorproduct=True) as may times as there are tensor factors, resp. until the expanded term does no longer change. This is however only reasonable in interactive session and not in algorithms.

### Code Fix
.expand relies on the method TensorProduct._eval_expand_tensorproduct(). The issue arises from an inprecise check in TensorProduct._eval_expand_tensorproduct() whether a recursive call is required; it fails when the creation of a TensorProduct object returns commutative (scalar) factors up front: in that case the constructor returns a Mul(c_factors, TensorProduct(..)).
I thus propose the following  code fix in TensorProduct._eval_expand_tensorproduct() in quantum/tensorproduct.py.  I have marked the four lines to be added / modified:
```
    def _eval_expand_tensorproduct(self, **hints):
                ...
                for aa in args[i].args:
                    tp = TensorProduct(*args[:i] + (aa,) + args[i + 1:])
                    c_part, nc_part = tp.args_cnc() #added
                    if len(nc_part)==1 and isinstance(nc_part[0], TensorProduct): #modified
                        nc_part = (nc_part[0]._eval_expand_tensorproduct(), ) #modified
                    add_args.append(Mul(*c_part)*Mul(*nc_part)) #modified
                break
                ...
```
The fix splits of commutative (scalar) factors from the tp returned. The TensorProduct object will be the one nc factor in nc_part (see TensorProduct.__new__ constructor), if any. Note that the constructor will return 0 if a tensor factor is 0, so there is no guarantee that tp contains a TensorProduct object (e.g. TensorProduct(U-U, U+V).

### GitHub Problem Description ###
Cannot parse Greek characters (and possibly others) in parse_mathematica
The old Mathematica parser `mathematica` in the package `sympy.parsing.mathematica` was able to parse e.g. Greek characters. Hence the following example works fine:
```
from sympy.parsing.mathematica import mathematica
mathematica('λ')
Out[]: 
λ
```

As of SymPy v. 1.11, the `mathematica` function is deprecated, and is replaced by `parse_mathematica`. This function, however, seems unable to handle the simple example above:
```
from sympy.parsing.mathematica import parse_mathematica
parse_mathematica('λ')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
File "<string>", line unknown
SyntaxError: unable to create a single AST for the expression
```

This appears to be due to a bug in `parse_mathematica`, which is why I have opened this issue.

Thanks in advance!

330|    def _get_layout(self, renderer):
331|        """
332|        Return the extent (bbox) of the text together with
333|        multiple-alignment information. Note that it returns an extent
334|        of a rotated text when necessary.
335|        """
336|        thisx, thisy = 0.0, 0.0
337|        text = self.get_text()
338|        lines = [text] if self.get_usetex() else text.split("\n")  # Not empty.
339|
340|        ws = []
341|        hs = []
342|        xs = []
343|        ys = []
344|
345|        # Full vertical extent of font, including ascenders and descenders:
346|        _, lp_h, lp_d = _get_text_metrics_with_cache(
347|            renderer, "lp", self._fontproperties,
348|            ismath="TeX" if self.get_usetex() else False, dpi=self.figure.dpi)
349|        min_dy = (lp_h - lp_d) * self._linespacing
350|
351|        for i, line in enumerate(lines):
352|            clean_line, ismath = self._preprocess_math(line)
353|            if clean_line:
354|                w, h, d = _get_text_metrics_with_cache(
355|                    renderer, clean_line, self._fontproperties,
356|                    ismath=ismath, dpi=self.figure.dpi)
357|            else:
358|                w = h = d = 0
359|
360|            # For multiline text, increase the line spacing when the text
361|            # net-height (excluding baseline) is larger than that of a "l"
362|            # (e.g., use of superscripts), which seems what TeX does.
363|            h = max(h, lp_h)
364|            d = max(d, lp_d)
365|
366|            ws.append(w)
367|            hs.append(h)
368|
369|            # Metrics of the last line that are needed later:
370|            baseline = (h - d) - thisy
371|
372|            if i == 0:
373|                # position at baseline
374|                thisy = -(h - d)
375|            else:
376|                # put baseline a good distance from bottom of previous line
377|                thisy -= max(min_dy, (h - d) * self._linespacing)
378|
379|            xs.append(thisx)  # == 0.
380|            ys.append(thisy)
381|
382|            thisy -= d
383|
384|        # Metrics of the last line that are needed later:
385|        descent = d
386|
387|        # Bounding box definition:
388|        width = max(ws)
389|        xmin = 0
390|        xmax = width
391|        ymax = 0
392|        ymin = ys[-1] - descent  # baseline of last line minus its descent
393|
394|        # get the rotation matrix
395|        M = Affine2D().rotate_deg(self.get_rotation())
396|
397|        # now offset the individual text lines within the box
398|        malign = self._get_multialignment()
399|        if malign == 'left':
400|            offset_layout = [(x, y) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)]
401|        elif malign == 'center':
402|            offset_layout = [(x + width / 2 - w / 2, y)
403|                             for x, y, w in zip(xs, ys, ws)]
404|        elif malign == 'right':
405|            offset_layout = [(x + width - w, y)
406|                             for x, y, w in zip(xs, ys, ws)]
407|
408|        # the corners of the unrotated bounding box
409|        corners_horiz = np.array(
410|            [(xmin, ymin), (xmin, ymax), (xmax, ymax), (xmax, ymin)])
411|
412|        # now rotate the bbox
413|        corners_rotated = M.transform(corners_horiz)
414|        # compute the bounds of the rotated box
415|        xmin = corners_rotated[:, 0].min()
416|        xmax = corners_rotated[:, 0].max()
417|        ymin = corners_rotated[:, 1].min()
418|        ymax = corners_rotated[:, 1].max()
419|        width = xmax - xmin
420|        height = ymax - ymin
421|
422|        # Now move the box to the target position offset the display
423|        # bbox by alignment
424|        halign = self._horizontalalignment
425|        valign = self._verticalalignment
426|
427|        rotation_mode = self.get_rotation_mode()
428|        if rotation_mode != "anchor":
429|            # compute the text location in display coords and the offsets
430|            # necessary to align the bbox with that location
431|            if halign == 'center':
432|                offsetx = (xmin + xmax) / 2
433|            elif halign == 'right':
434|                offsetx = xmax
435|            else:
436|                offsetx = xmin
437|
438|            if valign == 'center':
439|                offsety = (ymin + ymax) / 2
440|            elif valign == 'top':
441|                offsety = ymax
442|            elif valign == 'baseline':
443|                offsety = ymin + descent
444|            elif valign == 'center_baseline':
445|                offsety = ymin + height - baseline / 2.0
446|            else:
447|                offsety = ymin
448|        else:
449|            xmin1, ymin1 = corners_horiz[0]
450|            xmax1, ymax1 = corners_horiz[2]
451|
452|            if halign == 'center':
453|                offsetx = (xmin1 + xmax1) / 2.0
454|            elif halign == 'right':
455|                offsetx = xmax1
456|            else:
457|                offsetx = xmin1
458|
459|            if valign == 'center':
460|                offsety = (ymin1 + ymax1) / 2.0
461|            elif valign == 'top':
462|                offsety = ymax1
463|            elif valign == 'baseline':
464|                offsety = ymax1 - baseline
465|            elif valign == 'center_baseline':
466|                offsety = ymax1 - baseline / 2.0
467|            else:
468|                offsety = ymin1
469|
470|            offsetx, offsety = M.transform((offsetx, offsety))
471|
472|        xmin -= offsetx
473|        ymin -= offsety
474|
475|        bbox = Bbox.from_bounds(xmin, ymin, width, height)
476|
477|        # now rotate the positions around the first (x, y) position
478|        xys = M.transform(offset_layout) - (offsetx, offsety)
479|
480|        return bbox, list(zip(lines, zip(ws, hs), *xys.T)), descent

596|    def _get_wrap_line_width(self):
597|        """
598|        Return the maximum line width for wrapping text based on the current
599|        orientation.
600|        """
601|        x0, y0 = self.get_transform().transform(self.get_position())
602|        figure_box = self.get_figure().get_window_extent()
603|
604|        # Calculate available width based on text alignment
605|        alignment = self.get_horizontalalignment()
606|        self.set_rotation_mode('anchor')
607|        rotation = self.get_rotation()
608|
609|        left = self._get_dist_to_box(rotation, x0, y0, figure_box)
610|        right = self._get_dist_to_box(
611|            (180 + rotation) % 360, x0, y0, figure_box)
612|
613|        if alignment == 'left':
614|            line_width = left
615|        elif alignment == 'right':
616|            line_width = right
617|        else:
618|            line_width = 2 * min(left, right)
619|
620|        return line_width

622|    def _get_dist_to_box(self, rotation, x0, y0, figure_box):
623|        """
624|        Return the distance from the given points to the boundaries of a
625|        rotated box, in pixels.
626|        """
627|        if rotation > 270:
628|            quad = rotation - 270
629|            h1 = y0 / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
630|            h2 = (figure_box.x1 - x0) / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
631|        elif rotation > 180:
632|            quad = rotation - 180
633|            h1 = x0 / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
634|            h2 = y0 / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
635|        elif rotation > 90:
636|            quad = rotation - 90
637|            h1 = (figure_box.y1 - y0) / math.cos(math.radians(quad))
638|            h2 = x0 / math.cos(math.radians(90 - quad))
639|        else:
640|            h1 = (figure_box.x1 - x0) / math.cos(math.radians(rotation))
641|            h2 = (figure_box.y1 - y0) / math.cos(math.radians(90 - rotation))
642|
643|        return min(h1, h2)

655|    def _get_wrapped_text(self):
656|        """
657|        Return a copy of the text string with new lines added so that the text
658|        is wrapped relative to the parent figure (if `get_wrap` is True).
659|        """
660|        if not self.get_wrap():
661|            return self.get_text()
662|
663|        # Not fit to handle breaking up latex syntax correctly, so
664|        # ignore latex for now.
665|        if self.get_usetex():
666|            return self.get_text()
667|
668|        # Build the line incrementally, for a more accurate measure of length
669|        line_width = self._get_wrap_line_width()
670|        wrapped_lines = []
671|
672|        # New lines in the user's text force a split
673|        unwrapped_lines = self.get_text().split('\n')
674|
675|        # Now wrap each individual unwrapped line
676|        for unwrapped_line in unwrapped_lines:
677|
678|            sub_words = unwrapped_line.split(' ')
679|            # Remove items from sub_words as we go, so stop when empty
680|            while len(sub_words) > 0:
681|                if len(sub_words) == 1:
682|                    # Only one word, so just add it to the end
683|                    wrapped_lines.append(sub_words.pop(0))
684|                    continue
685|
686|                for i in range(2, len(sub_words) + 1):
687|                    # Get width of all words up to and including here
688|                    line = ' '.join(sub_words[:i])
689|                    current_width = self._get_rendered_text_width(line)
690|
691|                    # If all these words are too wide, append all not including
692|                    # last word
693|                    if current_width > line_width:
694|                        wrapped_lines.append(' '.join(sub_words[:i - 1]))
695|                        sub_words = sub_words[i - 1:]
696|                        break
697|
698|                    # Otherwise if all words fit in the width, append them all
699|                    elif i == len(sub_words):
700|                        wrapped_lines.append(' '.join(sub_words[:i]))
701|                        sub_words = []
702|                        break
703|
704|        return '\n'.join(wrapped_lines)

710|        if renderer is not None:

715|            return

717|        renderer.open_group('text', self.get_gid())
718|
719|        with self._cm_set(text=self._get_wrapped_text()):
720|            bbox, info, descent = self._get_layout(renderer)
721|            trans = self.get_transform()
722|
723|            # don't use self.get_position here, which refers to text
724|            # position in Text:
725|            posx = float(self.convert_xunits(self._x))
726|            posy = float(self.convert_yunits(self._y))
727|            posx, posy = trans.transform((posx, posy))
728|            if not np.isfinite(posx) or not np.isfinite(posy):
729|                _log.warning("posx and posy should be finite values")
730|                return
731|            canvasw, canvash = renderer.get_canvas_width_height()
732|
733|            # Update the location and size of the bbox
734|            # (`.patches.FancyBboxPatch`), and draw it.
735|            if self._bbox_patch:
736|                self.update_bbox_position_size(renderer)
737|                self._bbox_patch.draw(renderer)

739|            gc = renderer.new_gc()
740|            gc.set_foreground(self.get_color())
741|            gc.set_alpha(self.get_alpha())
742|            gc.set_url(self._url)
743|            self._set_gc_clip(gc)
744|
745|            angle = self.get_rotation()
746|
747|            for line, wh, x, y in info:
748|
749|                mtext = self if len(info) == 1 else None
750|                x = x + posx
751|                y = y + posy
752|                if renderer.flipy():
753|                    y = canvash - y
754|                clean_line, ismath = self._preprocess_math(line)

756|                if self.get_path_effects():
757|                    from matplotlib.patheffects import PathEffectRenderer
758|                    textrenderer = PathEffectRenderer(
759|                        self.get_path_effects(), renderer)
760|                else:
761|                    textrenderer = renderer

763|                if self.get_usetex():

765|                                          self._fontproperties, angle,
766|                                          mtext=mtext)
767|                else:
768|                    textrenderer.draw_text(gc, x, y, clean_line,
769|                                           self._fontproperties, angle,
770|                                           ismath=ismath, mtext=mtext)
771|
772|        gc.restore()
773|        renderer.close_group('text')

### GitHub Problem Description ###
[Bug]: using clf and pyplot.draw in range slider on_changed callback blocks input to widgets
### Bug summary

When using clear figure, adding new widgets and then redrawing the current figure in the on_changed callback of a range slider the inputs to all the widgets in the figure are blocked. When doing the same in the button callback on_clicked, everything works fine.

### Code for reproduction

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as pyplot
import matplotlib.widgets as widgets

def onchanged(values):
    print("on changed")
    print(values)
    pyplot.clf()
    addElements()
    pyplot.draw()

def onclick(e):
    print("on click")
    pyplot.clf()
    addElements()
    pyplot.draw()

def addElements():
    ax = pyplot.axes([0.1, 0.45, 0.8, 0.1])
    global slider
    slider = widgets.RangeSlider(ax, "Test", valmin=1, valmax=10, valinit=(1, 10))
    slider.on_changed(onchanged)
    ax = pyplot.axes([0.1, 0.30, 0.8, 0.1])
    global button
    button = widgets.Button(ax, "Test")
    button.on_clicked(onclick)

addElements()

pyplot.show()
```


### Actual outcome

The widgets can't receive any input from a mouse click, when redrawing in the on_changed callback of a range Slider. 
When using a button, there is no problem.

### Expected outcome

The range slider callback on_changed behaves the same as the button callback on_clicked.

### Additional information

The problem also occurred on Manjaro with:
- Python version: 3.10.9
- Matplotlib version: 3.6.2
- Matplotlib backend: QtAgg
- Installation of matplotlib via Linux package manager

493|    def update_normal(self, mappable):
494|        """
495|        Update solid patches, lines, etc.
496|
497|        This is meant to be called when the norm of the image or contour plot
498|        to which this colorbar belongs changes.

500|        If the norm on the mappable is different than before, this resets the
501|        locator and formatter for the axis, so if these have been customized,
502|        they will need to be customized again.  However, if the norm only
503|        changes values of *vmin*, *vmax* or *cmap* then the old formatter
504|        and locator will be preserved.
505|        """
506|        _log.debug('colorbar update normal %r %r', mappable.norm, self.norm)
507|        self.mappable = mappable
508|        self.set_alpha(mappable.get_alpha())
509|        self.cmap = mappable.cmap
510|        if mappable.norm != self.norm:
511|            self.norm = mappable.norm
512|            self._reset_locator_formatter_scale()
513|
514|        self._draw_all()
515|        if isinstance(self.mappable, contour.ContourSet):
516|            CS = self.mappable
517|            if not CS.filled:
518|                self.add_lines(CS)
519|        self.stale = True

529|    def _draw_all(self):
530|        """
531|        Calculate any free parameters based on the current cmap and norm,
532|        and do all the drawing.
533|        """
534|        if self.orientation == 'vertical':
535|            if mpl.rcParams['ytick.minor.visible']:
536|                self.minorticks_on()
537|        else:
538|            if mpl.rcParams['xtick.minor.visible']:
539|                self.minorticks_on()
540|        self._long_axis().set(label_position=self.ticklocation,
541|                              ticks_position=self.ticklocation)
542|        self._short_axis().set_ticks([])
543|        self._short_axis().set_ticks([], minor=True)
544|
545|        # Set self._boundaries and self._values, including extensions.
546|        # self._boundaries are the edges of each square of color, and
547|        # self._values are the value to map into the norm to get the
548|        # color:
549|        self._process_values()
550|        # Set self.vmin and self.vmax to first and last boundary, excluding
551|        # extensions:
552|        self.vmin, self.vmax = self._boundaries[self._inside][[0, -1]]
553|        # Compute the X/Y mesh.
554|        X, Y = self._mesh()
555|        # draw the extend triangles, and shrink the inner axes to accommodate.
556|        # also adds the outline path to self.outline spine:
557|        self._do_extends()
558|        lower, upper = self.vmin, self.vmax
559|        if self._long_axis().get_inverted():
560|            # If the axis is inverted, we need to swap the vmin/vmax
561|            lower, upper = upper, lower
562|        if self.orientation == 'vertical':
563|            self.ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
564|            self.ax.set_ylim(lower, upper)
565|        else:
566|            self.ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
567|            self.ax.set_xlim(lower, upper)
568|
569|        # set up the tick locators and formatters.  A bit complicated because
570|        # boundary norms + uniform spacing requires a manual locator.
571|        self.update_ticks()
572|
573|        if self._filled:
574|            ind = np.arange(len(self._values))
575|            if self._extend_lower():
576|                ind = ind[1:]
577|            if self._extend_upper():
578|                ind = ind[:-1]
579|            self._add_solids(X, Y, self._values[ind, np.newaxis])
580|
581|    def _add_solids(self, X, Y, C):
582|        """Draw the colors; optionally add separators."""
583|        # Cleanup previously set artists.
584|        if self.solids is not None:
585|            self.solids.remove()
586|        for solid in self.solids_patches:
587|            solid.remove()
588|        # Add new artist(s), based on mappable type.  Use individual patches if
589|        # hatching is needed, pcolormesh otherwise.
590|        mappable = getattr(self, 'mappable', None)
591|        if (isinstance(mappable, contour.ContourSet)
592|                and any(hatch is not None for hatch in mappable.hatches)):
593|            self._add_solids_patches(X, Y, C, mappable)
594|        else:
595|            self.solids = self.ax.pcolormesh(
596|                X, Y, C, cmap=self.cmap, norm=self.norm, alpha=self.alpha,
597|                edgecolors='none', shading='flat')
598|            if not self.drawedges:
599|                if len(self._y) >= self.n_rasterize:
600|                    self.solids.set_rasterized(True)
601|        self._update_dividers()
602|
603|    def _update_dividers(self):
604|        if not self.drawedges:
605|            self.dividers.set_segments([])
606|            return
607|        # Place all *internal* dividers.
608|        if self.orientation == 'vertical':
609|            lims = self.ax.get_ylim()
610|            bounds = (lims[0] < self._y) & (self._y < lims[1])
611|        else:
612|            lims = self.ax.get_xlim()
613|            bounds = (lims[0] < self._y) & (self._y < lims[1])
614|        y = self._y[bounds]
615|        # And then add outer dividers if extensions are on.
616|        if self._extend_lower():
617|            y = np.insert(y, 0, lims[0])
618|        if self._extend_upper():
619|            y = np.append(y, lims[1])
620|        X, Y = np.meshgrid([0, 1], y)
621|        if self.orientation == 'vertical':
622|            segments = np.dstack([X, Y])
623|        else:
624|            segments = np.dstack([Y, X])
625|        self.dividers.set_segments(segments)
626|
627|    def _add_solids_patches(self, X, Y, C, mappable):
628|        hatches = mappable.hatches * (len(C) + 1)  # Have enough hatches.
629|        if self._extend_lower():
630|            # remove first hatch that goes into the extend patch
631|            hatches = hatches[1:]
632|        patches = []
633|        for i in range(len(X) - 1):
634|            xy = np.array([[X[i, 0], Y[i, 1]],
635|                           [X[i, 1], Y[i, 0]],
636|                           [X[i + 1, 1], Y[i + 1, 0]],
637|                           [X[i + 1, 0], Y[i + 1, 1]]])
638|            patch = mpatches.PathPatch(mpath.Path(xy),
639|                                       facecolor=self.cmap(self.norm(C[i][0])),
640|                                       hatch=hatches[i], linewidth=0,
641|                                       antialiased=False, alpha=self.alpha)
642|            self.ax.add_patch(patch)
643|            patches.append(patch)
644|        self.solids_patches = patches
645|
646|    def _do_extends(self, ax=None):
647|        """
648|        Add the extend tri/rectangles on the outside of the axes.
649|
650|        ax is unused, but required due to the callbacks on xlim/ylim changed
651|        """
652|        # Clean up any previous extend patches
653|        for patch in self._extend_patches:
654|            patch.remove()
655|        self._extend_patches = []
656|        # extend lengths are fraction of the *inner* part of colorbar,
657|        # not the total colorbar:
658|        _, extendlen = self._proportional_y()
659|        bot = 0 - (extendlen[0] if self._extend_lower() else 0)
660|        top = 1 + (extendlen[1] if self._extend_upper() else 0)
661|
662|        # xyout is the outline of the colorbar including the extend patches:
663|        if not self.extendrect:
664|            # triangle:
665|            xyout = np.array([[0, 0], [0.5, bot], [1, 0],
666|                              [1, 1], [0.5, top], [0, 1], [0, 0]])
667|        else:
668|            # rectangle:
669|            xyout = np.array([[0, 0], [0, bot], [1, bot], [1, 0],
670|                              [1, 1], [1, top], [0, top], [0, 1],
671|                              [0, 0]])
672|
673|        if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
674|            xyout = xyout[:, ::-1]
675|
676|        # xyout is the path for the spine:
677|        self.outline.set_xy(xyout)
678|        if not self._filled:
679|            return
680|
681|        # Make extend triangles or rectangles filled patches.  These are
682|        # defined in the outer parent axes' coordinates:
683|        mappable = getattr(self, 'mappable', None)
684|        if (isinstance(mappable, contour.ContourSet)
685|                and any(hatch is not None for hatch in mappable.hatches)):
686|            hatches = mappable.hatches * (len(self._y) + 1)
687|        else:
688|            hatches = [None] * (len(self._y) + 1)
689|
690|        if self._extend_lower():
691|            if not self.extendrect:
692|                # triangle
693|                xy = np.array([[0, 0], [0.5, bot], [1, 0]])
694|            else:
695|                # rectangle
696|                xy = np.array([[0, 0], [0, bot], [1., bot], [1, 0]])
697|            if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
698|                xy = xy[:, ::-1]
699|            # add the patch
700|            val = -1 if self._long_axis().get_inverted() else 0
701|            color = self.cmap(self.norm(self._values[val]))
702|            patch = mpatches.PathPatch(
703|                mpath.Path(xy), facecolor=color, alpha=self.alpha,
704|                linewidth=0, antialiased=False,
705|                transform=self.ax.transAxes,
706|                hatch=hatches[0], clip_on=False,
707|                # Place it right behind the standard patches, which is
708|                # needed if we updated the extends
709|                zorder=np.nextafter(self.ax.patch.zorder, -np.inf))
710|            self.ax.add_patch(patch)
711|            self._extend_patches.append(patch)
712|            # remove first hatch that goes into the extend patch
713|            hatches = hatches[1:]
714|        if self._extend_upper():
715|            if not self.extendrect:
716|                # triangle
717|                xy = np.array([[0, 1], [0.5, top], [1, 1]])
718|            else:
719|                # rectangle
720|                xy = np.array([[0, 1], [0, top], [1, top], [1, 1]])
721|            if self.orientation == 'horizontal':
722|                xy = xy[:, ::-1]
723|            # add the patch
724|            val = 0 if self._long_axis().get_inverted() else -1
725|            color = self.cmap(self.norm(self._values[val]))
726|            hatch_idx = len(self._y) - 1
727|            patch = mpatches.PathPatch(
728|                mpath.Path(xy), facecolor=color, alpha=self.alpha,
729|                linewidth=0, antialiased=False,
730|                transform=self.ax.transAxes, hatch=hatches[hatch_idx],
731|                clip_on=False,
732|                # Place it right behind the standard patches, which is
733|                # needed if we updated the extends
734|                zorder=np.nextafter(self.ax.patch.zorder, -np.inf))
735|            self.ax.add_patch(patch)
736|            self._extend_patches.append(patch)
737|
738|        self._update_dividers()

740|    def add_lines(self, *args, **kwargs):
741|        """
742|        Draw lines on the colorbar.
743|
744|        The lines are appended to the list :attr:`lines`.
745|
746|        Parameters
747|        ----------
748|        levels : array-like
749|            The positions of the lines.
750|        colors : color or list of colors
751|            Either a single color applying to all lines or one color value for
752|            each line.
753|        linewidths : float or array-like
754|            Either a single linewidth applying to all lines or one linewidth
755|            for each line.
756|        erase : bool, default: True
757|            Whether to remove any previously added lines.
758|
759|        Notes
760|        -----
761|        Alternatively, this method can also be called with the signature
762|        ``colorbar.add_lines(contour_set, erase=True)``, in which case
763|        *levels*, *colors*, and *linewidths* are taken from *contour_set*.
764|        """
765|        params = _api.select_matching_signature(
766|            [lambda self, CS, erase=True: locals(),
767|             lambda self, levels, colors, linewidths, erase=True: locals()],
768|            self, *args, **kwargs)
769|        if "CS" in params:
770|            self, CS, erase = params.values()
771|            if not isinstance(CS, contour.ContourSet) or CS.filled:
772|                raise ValueError("If a single artist is passed to add_lines, "
773|                                 "it must be a ContourSet of lines")
774|            # TODO: Make colorbar lines auto-follow changes in contour lines.
775|            return self.add_lines(
776|                CS.levels,
777|                [c[0] for c in CS.tcolors],
778|                [t[0] for t in CS.tlinewidths],
779|                erase=erase)
780|        else:
781|            self, levels, colors, linewidths, erase = params.values()
782|
783|        y = self._locate(levels)
784|        rtol = (self._y[-1] - self._y[0]) * 1e-10
785|        igood = (y < self._y[-1] + rtol) & (y > self._y[0] - rtol)
786|        y = y[igood]
787|        if np.iterable(colors):
788|            colors = np.asarray(colors)[igood]
789|        if np.iterable(linewidths):
790|            linewidths = np.asarray(linewidths)[igood]
791|        X, Y = np.meshgrid([0, 1], y)
792|        if self.orientation == 'vertical':
793|            xy = np.stack([X, Y], axis=-1)
794|        else:
795|            xy = np.stack([Y, X], axis=-1)
796|        col = collections.LineCollection(xy, linewidths=linewidths,
797|                                         colors=colors)
798|
799|        if erase and self.lines:
800|            for lc in self.lines:
801|                lc.remove()
802|            self.lines = []
803|        self.lines.append(col)
804|
805|        # make a clip path that is just a linewidth bigger than the axes...
806|        fac = np.max(linewidths) / 72
807|        xy = np.array([[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1], [0, 0]])
808|        inches = self.ax.get_figure().dpi_scale_trans
809|        # do in inches:
810|        xy = inches.inverted().transform(self.ax.transAxes.transform(xy))
811|        xy[[0, 1, 4], 1] -= fac
812|        xy[[2, 3], 1] += fac
813|        # back to axes units...
814|        xy = self.ax.transAxes.inverted().transform(inches.transform(xy))
815|        col.set_clip_path(mpath.Path(xy, closed=True),
816|                          self.ax.transAxes)
817|        self.ax.add_collection(col)
818|        self.stale = True

823|        """
824|        # Get the locator and formatter; defaults to self._locator if not None.
825|        self._get_ticker_locator_formatter()
826|        self._long_axis().set_major_locator(self._locator)
827|        self._long_axis().set_minor_locator(self._minorlocator)

830|    def _get_ticker_locator_formatter(self):
831|        """
832|        Return the ``locator`` and ``formatter`` of the colorbar.
833|
834|        If they have not been defined (i.e. are *None*), the formatter and
835|        locator are retrieved from the axis, or from the value of the
836|        boundaries for a boundary norm.
837|
838|        Called by update_ticks...
839|        """
840|        locator = self._locator
841|        formatter = self._formatter
842|        minorlocator = self._minorlocator
843|        if isinstance(self.norm, colors.BoundaryNorm):
844|            b = self.norm.boundaries
845|            if locator is None:
846|                locator = ticker.FixedLocator(b, nbins=10)
847|            if minorlocator is None:
848|                minorlocator = ticker.FixedLocator(b)
849|        elif isinstance(self.norm, colors.NoNorm):
850|            if locator is None:
851|                # put ticks on integers between the boundaries of NoNorm
852|                nv = len(self._values)
853|                base = 1 + int(nv / 10)
854|                locator = ticker.IndexLocator(base=base, offset=.5)
855|        elif self.boundaries is not None:
856|            b = self._boundaries[self._inside]
857|            if locator is None:
858|                locator = ticker.FixedLocator(b, nbins=10)
859|        else:  # most cases:
860|            if locator is None:
861|                # we haven't set the locator explicitly, so use the default
862|                # for this axis:
863|                locator = self._long_axis().get_major_locator()
864|            if minorlocator is None:
865|                minorlocator = self._long_axis().get_minor_locator()
866|
867|        if minorlocator is None:
868|            minorlocator = ticker.NullLocator()
869|
870|        if formatter is None:
871|            formatter = self._long_axis().get_major_formatter()
872|
873|        self._locator = locator
874|        self._formatter = formatter
875|        self._minorlocator = minorlocator
876|        _log.debug('locator: %r', locator)

878|    def set_ticks(self, ticks, *, labels=None, minor=False, **kwargs):
879|        """
880|        Set tick locations.
881|
882|        Parameters
883|        ----------
884|        ticks : list of floats
885|            List of tick locations.
886|        labels : list of str, optional
887|            List of tick labels. If not set, the labels show the data value.
888|        minor : bool, default: False
889|            If ``False``, set the major ticks; if ``True``, the minor ticks.
890|        **kwargs
891|            `.Text` properties for the labels. These take effect only if you
892|            pass *labels*. In other cases, please use `~.Axes.tick_params`.
893|        """
894|        if np.iterable(ticks):
895|            self._long_axis().set_ticks(ticks, labels=labels, minor=minor,
896|                                        **kwargs)
897|            self._locator = self._long_axis().get_major_locator()

When an axis is shared with another its registered "xlim_changed" callbacks does not get called when the change is induced by a shared axis (via sharex=).

I'm very new to matplotlib, so perhaps there is a good reason for this? emit=False seems to disable both continued "inheritance" of axis (why?) and triggering of change callbacks (looking at the code above).

It seems like one would at least want to trigger the xlim_changed callbacks as they would be intended to react to any change in axis limits.

Edit: Setting emit=True seems to introduce a recursion issue (not sure why but as inheritance seems to be passed along anyway it doesn't really matter). 1177|        # and use it if it's available (else just use 0..1)

1179|    def _set_lim(self, v0, v1, *, emit=True, auto):
1180|        """
1181|        Set view limits.
1182|
1183|        This method is a helper for the Axes ``set_xlim``, ``set_ylim``, and
1184|        ``set_zlim`` methods.
1185|
1186|        Parameters
1187|        ----------
1188|        v0, v1 : float
1189|            The view limits.  (Passing *v0* as a (low, high) pair is not
1190|            supported; normalization must occur in the Axes setters.)
1191|        emit : bool, default: True
1192|            Whether to notify observers of limit change.
1193|        auto : bool or None, default: False
1194|            Whether to turn on autoscaling of the x-axis. True turns on, False
1195|            turns off, None leaves unchanged.
1196|        """
1197|        name = self._get_axis_name()
1198|
1199|        self.axes._process_unit_info([(name, (v0, v1))], convert=False)
1200|        v0 = self.axes._validate_converted_limits(v0, self.convert_units)
1201|        v1 = self.axes._validate_converted_limits(v1, self.convert_units)
1202|
1203|        if v0 is None or v1 is None:
1204|            # Axes init calls set_xlim(0, 1) before get_xlim() can be called,
1205|            # so only grab the limits if we really need them.
1206|            old0, old1 = self.get_view_interval()
1207|            if v0 is None:
1208|                v0 = old0
1209|            if v1 is None:
1210|                v1 = old1
1211|
1212|        if self.get_scale() == 'log' and (v0 <= 0 or v1 <= 0):
1213|            # Axes init calls set_xlim(0, 1) before get_xlim() can be called,
1214|            # so only grab the limits if we really need them.
1215|            old0, old1 = self.get_view_interval()
1216|            if v0 <= 0:
1217|                _api.warn_external(f"Attempt to set non-positive {name}lim on "
1218|                                   f"a log-scaled axis will be ignored.")
1219|                v0 = old0
1220|            if v1 <= 0:
1221|                _api.warn_external(f"Attempt to set non-positive {name}lim on "
1222|                                   f"a log-scaled axis will be ignored.")
1223|                v1 = old1
1224|        if v0 == v1:
1225|            _api.warn_external(
1226|                f"Attempting to set identical low and high {name}lims "
1227|                f"makes transformation singular; automatically expanding.")
1228|        reverse = bool(v0 > v1)  # explicit cast needed for python3.8+np.bool_.
1229|        v0, v1 = self.get_major_locator().nonsingular(v0, v1)
1230|        v0, v1 = self.limit_range_for_scale(v0, v1)
1231|        v0, v1 = sorted([v0, v1], reverse=bool(reverse))
1232|
1233|        self.set_view_interval(v0, v1, ignore=True)
1234|        # Mark viewlims as no longer stale without triggering an autoscale.
1235|        for ax in self._get_shared_axes():
1236|            ax._stale_viewlims[name] = False
1237|        if auto is not None:
1238|            self._set_autoscale_on(bool(auto))
1239|
1240|        if emit:
1241|            self.axes.callbacks.process(f"{name}lim_changed", self.axes)
1242|            # Call all of the other axes that are shared with this one
1243|            for other in self._get_shared_axes():
1244|                if other is not self.axes:
1245|                    other._axis_map[name]._set_lim(
1246|                        v0, v1, emit=False, auto=auto)
1247|                    if other.figure != self.figure:
1248|                        other.figure.canvas.draw_idle()
1249|
1250|        self.stale = True
1251|        return v0, v1

1258|    def _update_ticks(self):
1259|        """
1260|        Update ticks (position and labels) using the current data interval of
1261|        the axes.  Return the list of ticks that will be drawn.
1262|        """
1263|        major_locs = self.get_majorticklocs()
1264|        major_labels = self.major.formatter.format_ticks(major_locs)
1265|        major_ticks = self.get_major_ticks(len(major_locs))
1266|        for tick, loc, label in zip(major_ticks, major_locs, major_labels):
1267|            tick.update_position(loc)
1268|            tick.label1.set_text(label)
1269|            tick.label2.set_text(label)
1270|        minor_locs = self.get_minorticklocs()
1271|        minor_labels = self.minor.formatter.format_ticks(minor_locs)
1272|        minor_ticks = self.get_minor_ticks(len(minor_locs))
1273|        for tick, loc, label in zip(minor_ticks, minor_locs, minor_labels):
1274|            tick.update_position(loc)
1275|            tick.label1.set_text(label)
1276|            tick.label2.set_text(label)
1277|        ticks = [*major_ticks, *minor_ticks]
1278|
1279|        view_low, view_high = self.get_view_interval()
1280|        if view_low > view_high:
1281|            view_low, view_high = view_high, view_low
1282|
1283|        interval_t = self.get_transform().transform([view_low, view_high])
1284|
1285|        ticks_to_draw = []
1286|        for tick in ticks:
1287|            try:
1288|                loc_t = self.get_transform().transform(tick.get_loc())
1289|            except AssertionError:
1290|                # transforms.transform doesn't allow masked values but
1291|                # some scales might make them, so we need this try/except.
1292|                pass
1293|            else:
1294|                if mtransforms._interval_contains_close(interval_t, loc_t):
1295|                    ticks_to_draw.append(tick)
1296|
1297|        return ticks_to_draw
